Niño Lawrence Morales
Juanito Mendoza
Floralyn Simbulan
Christina Mae Del Rosario Pineda

blocks.text: Co’s staff members, John Paul Estrada and Mark Tecsay, were also charged.
The case centers on a project for the construction of a riverbank protection structure along the Balagtas River in Barangay San Juan, Balagtas, Bulacan.
The said project was awarded to SYMS Construction Trading. The revised contract was valued at approximately P77.2 million.
According to the Ombudsman, the project commenced on Feb. 24, 2025, and was certified as 100% complete by May 2, 2025.
However, a subsequent physical inspection revealed that the flood-control structure was entirely nonexistent.
The Ombudsman pointed to an "implied conspiracy" among the accused, detailing how kickbacks collected by Alcantara from contractors were allegedly delivered in advance to Co.
In exchange, Co ensured the insertion of the project into the National Expenditure Program (NEP) and its subsequent funding in the General Appropriations Act.
"Co’s participation was therefore necessary or indispensable in this elaborate scheme of embezzling funds intended for flood control projects," the Ombudsman’s statement read.

“The modus did not end after the delivery of the advance payment to Co. The project was eventually awarded to SYMS which was owned by Santos. However, and which is apparent in the scheme used by the respondents, there was no intention to actually complete the project,” the ruling added.
The anti-graft body also pointed out that the officials who were tasked with inspecting, auditing and approving the project repeatedly failed to perform their duties.
The agency noted that these oversight failures were far too systematic to be brushed off as simple oversights or isolated mistakes.

“Here, respondents acted with evident bad faith and/or gross inexcusable negligence when they issued the pertinent documents and certifications that led to the diversion of public funds… for a project that turned out to be non-existent or incomplete. The repeated failure to exercise due diligence is very telling,” the Ombudsman said.
The malversation case was raffled to the Sandiganbayan Fourth Division, while the graft case was raffled to the Fifth Division.
Partial dismissals

While proceeding with the graft and malversation charges, the Ombudsman dismissed the charge for violation of Section 3(b) of RA 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, against Co, Alcantara, Estrada, and Tecsay due to lack of probable cause.
Meanwhile, a separate perjury charge against SYMS contractor Sally Santos was referred back to the Department of Justice for proper disposition.
Co, who is currently at large, is also facing graft and malversation charges before the Sandiganbayan for the P289.5-million flood control project in Oriental Mindoro.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo spreads to 2 new health zones with a total of 60 areas now affected
articles.summary: BUNIA, Congo (AP) — The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history has spread to two new health zones in eastern Congo, with a total of 60 now affected, according to the latest government figures…

blocks.text: BUNIA, Congo (AP) — The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history has spread to two new health zones in eastern Congo, with a total of 60 now affected, according to the latest government figures published on Friday.

blocks.caption: FILE - Health workers tend to an Ebola patient at the Rwampara Treatment Center in Ituri, Congo, Thursday, June 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Moses Sawasawa, file)

blocks.text: FILE - Health workers tend to an Ebola patient at the Rwampara Treatment Center in Ituri, Congo, Thursday, June 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Moses Sawasawa, file)

The two new zones affected are Biena and Manguredjipa in Congo's North Kivu province, where the case fatality rate is much higher than the overall rate of 48%, due in part to delayed response efforts, according to Congo's Ministry of Health data.
It said the outbreak has recorded 5,794 confirmed cases, including 2,786 deaths, as it is spreading at an unprecedented speed, faster than efforts to track and slow it.

The outbreak is spreading under extremely difficult conditions, fueled by insecurity, displacement, a health workers' strike and intense population movements. The World Health Organization has said that it remains out of control and is on track to surpass the 2014-2016 West Africa Ebola outbreak, the deadliest on record, which killed more than 11,000 people, primarily in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

On Thursday, Congo began vaccinating health workers and other front-line workers with the Ervebo vaccine that was effective in past Ebola outbreaks caused by a different, more common type called Zaire.
Clinical trials are underway to find a licensed vaccine for the rare Bundibugyo virus that is causing the current outbreak and which has no approved vaccines or treatments.

Although the current outbreak was declared in mid-May, officials believe it had been spreading since February. It has spread from three health zones to nearly 60, with most cases and deaths occurring outside the network of monitored contacts and within communities.

Efforts to bring the outbreak under control — from limited public gatherings to social distancing and airport closures — have disrupted life in the six affected provinces, particularly Ituri, which has been ravaged by rebel violence.
The government has introduced measures, including installing health and sanitary equipment at some locations, but advocacy groups say more needs to be done to build trust within the community.
The majority of cases are concentrated in the northeastern Ituri province, which accounts for more than 83% of cases, according to the latest government figures.
While neighboring Uganda declared itself free of Ebola last month, the risk of further cross-border spread remains, WHO said Wednesday.

WHO expert Marie Roseline Belizaire said that the Central African Republic is now considered the country at highest risk of spillover, followed closely by South Sudan, as the outbreak in eastern Congo has expanded toward border areas.

articles.title: What 'The Odyssey' can teach us about climate chaos
articles.summary: The Bronze Age collapse may have started with a water crisis. Today’s droughts raise the unsettling question of whether it could happen again.

image.caption: Homer's epic, "The Odyssey," is set against a backdrop of civilisational collapseImage: Cinema Publishers Collection/IMAGO

blocks.text: Christopher Nolan's latest blockbuster has drawn tens of millions of viewers into a world of stormy seas and cities on fire.
Minus the monsters, that world is based in reality. "The Odyssey" — a post-Trojan War survival story — is set during the Bronze Age collapse of civilization.
A new study links that collapse to a severe climate shift. And the authors warn of "implications for the future."
Scientists have long known about a mysterious and severe drought that struck more than 3,000 years ago, overlapping with the disintegration of kingdoms and states across the Mediterranean.
Ancient Epic: The Odyssey on Film
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Research published last month sheds light on the potential cause of that drought: A slow drying trend and a quicker natural cycle of dry weather stacked on top of each other.

By the late Bronze Age, the West African monsoon system had been shrinking for thousands of years, turning a green Sahara into desert. Less rain over Africa meant less over the Mediterranean. That trend amplified when the region hit a dry spell caused by natural climate cycles from the Atlantic, which saw the region swing between decades-long wet and dry periods.
Katherine Power, the Stockholm University scientist who led the study, said the environment at the time could explain the mass migration and conflicts of the Odyssey's era.
For decades, scholars have speculated on the reason for the large-scale movement during this time — which is also referred to as the period of the so-called Sea Peoples.

blocks.caption: A copy of a fresco from the Central Court at Knossos, Greece, one of the palace cities abandoned during the Late Bronze AgeImage: World History Archive/picture alliance

blocks.text: Archeologists argue that climate shifts could help explain the migration and political collapse at the end of the Bronze Age. The new findings add puzzle pieces.
"We don't know necessarily why those people moved," Power said. "But if we can say, 'hey, the climate was getting worse and worse to survive,' that could be a potential reason."
'A perfect storm of calamities'

And that, she says, is relevant to today. Europe's major rivers are at record lows, and drought is creating conditions for devastating wildfires as well as fueling historic crop-loss. That includes France's lowest maize harvest in 50 years.

blocks.caption: Heatwaves and drought have wreaked havoc with cropsImage: Patricia Huchot-Boissier/ABACAPRESS/IMAGO

blocks.text: The same cycles of wetting and drying from the Atlantic are still at play, but they're now happening in the context of a world that's heating as a result of humans burning oil, gas and coal.
"I think it is even more alarming and even more of a threat," Power said.
But does what happened then give insights into what might happen now?

Eric H. Cline, archeologist at George Washington University, who wrote a book on the roots of the Bronze Age crisis, said drought and disease were part of the "perfect storm of calamities" that led to societal downfall.
He sees parallels to today. In an email to DW, he said "we should be very concerned" about climate change as a stressor for the collapse of civilization. "That fear is not too dramatic at all."
He added that on his most optimistic days, he believes "we will come to our senses and sidestep that possibility at some point."
How climate change is teaming up with 'Super El Nino'
Was there a trigger moment for the collapse?
Power's research sought to explore what patterns might lie behind isolated Bronze Age drought events.

They started by examining plant spores, ice cores, cave stones, and other natural records that pointed to drought. Then, she and co-author Stockholm paleoclimate scientist Qiong Zhang turned to modeling to get a broader picture.

Their model looked at the whole planet, overlaid with a grid, each cell covering a roughly 125-kilometer (78-mile) area. A supercomputer then calculated the conditions in each of these cells, for every month, across thousands of years. That let the scientists look at the entire Mediterranean.
"We're not now stuck with just one core or one cave," Power said. "We can see farther afield and build a whole picture."

blocks.caption: The ruins of Tiryns, a Greek palace city that declined during the Bronze Age Collapse amid drought and regional upheavalImage: Ian Murray/imageBROKER/IMAGO

blocks.text: What they found was not a single event that dramatically and suddenly changed the climate. Instead, shorter cycles of wetting and drying lined up with a longer warming trend.

"When we are looking for connections between climate changes and civilization changes, we often are looking for that big, huge, abrupt, catastrophic event," Power said, adding that it is "slow, gradual changes that push a society over a threshold.”
She said it could have been a steady fall in water supply that led to a slow decline in crops, which prompted people to migrate, triggering conflict.

"It doesn't take very much to push a society over the threshold that they're comfortable with," Power said. "What if you add something more to the mix? Maybe then that pushes you a bit farther, and you can't quite recover from that."
Edited by: Tamsin Walker

articles.title: Ombudsman files graft, malversation raps vs Co, DPWH execs over ₱77-M Bulacan flood control project
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman (OMB) has filed graft and malversation charges against former Ako Bicol Party-list Rep. Elizaldy “Zaldy” Co and several Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)…

blocks.text: (PHOTO: ZALDY CO FACEBOOK PAGE)

The Office of the Ombudsman (OMB) has filed graft and malversation charges against former Ako Bicol Party-list Rep. Elizaldy “Zaldy” Co and several Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials over an allegedly anomalous ₱77-million flood control project in Balagtas, Bulacan, which the anti-graft body said an inspection found to be non-existent.

In a statement on Friday, Aug. 28, the OMB said it found probable cause to charge Co and DPWH officials Henry Alcantara, Brice Ericson Diaz Hernandez, Arjay Salvador Domasig, Jaypee De Leon Mendoza, Niño Lawrence Vergara Morales, Juanito Coronel Mendoza, Floralyn Yutuc Simbulan, and Christina Mae Del Rosario Pineda.

The probable-cause finding covered one count of malversation of public funds through falsification of public documents under Article 217, in relation to Article 171(4), of the Revised Penal Code and one count of violation of Section 3(e) of Republic Act No. 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.
Alcantara, however, was not included in the information filed before the Sandiganbayan because he had been admitted into the Witness Protection Program.
Meanwhile, the anti-graft body said Co’s staff members, John Paul Estrada and Mark Tecsay, were also included in the indictment.
The case involves the construction of a riverbank protection structure along the Balagtas River in Purok 4, Barangay San Juan, Balagtas, Bulacan, under Contract ID No. 25CC0155.
According to the OMB, the project was awarded to SYMS Construction Trading and had a revised contract amount of approximately ₱77.2 million.
A subsequent inspection found that the flood-control structure did not exist despite documents and certifications indicating that the project had been completed, the OMB said.
“The project supposedly started last February 24, 2025 and was declared to be 100% accomplished on May 2, 2025. However, upon inspection, it was non-existent,” the ruling stated.
The OMB said its finding of probable cause was based on a series of approvals and certifications that allowed the release of public funds despite glaring irregularities.

“The repeated approvals of the payments to SYMS, in spite of the glaring irregularities in the Monthly Certificates of Payment (MCPs) and Statements of Work Accomplished (SWAs), are strong indication of their participation in the devious schemes of misappropriating the funds for flood control projects,” the resolution read.
According to the OMB, the respondents’ collective actions indicated the presence of an implied conspiracy.

“In exchange for the kickbacks collected by Alcantara from contractors and delivered in advance to Co, the latter ensured that the project will be inserted in the NEP and eventually funded in the General Appropriations Act (GAA). Co’s participation was therefore necessary or indispensable in this elaborate scheme of embezzling funds intended for flood control projects,” the resolution stated.

“The modus did not end after the delivery of the advance payment to Co. The project was eventually awarded to SYMS which was owned by Santos. However, and which is apparent in the scheme used by the respondents, there was no intention to actually complete the project,” the ruling added.

The OMB also cited the repeated failure of officials responsible for reviewing, inspecting, and certifying the project to exercise the required diligence, saying these could not be considered ordinary lapses or isolated errors.

“Here, respondents acted with evident bad faith and/or gross inexcusable negligence when they issued the pertinent documents and certifications that led to the diversion of public funds… for a project that turned out to be non-existent or incomplete. The repeated failure to exercise due diligence is very telling,” the resolution stated.

The resolution found that the respondents’ actions, taken together, demonstrated their direct and active involvement from the start of the project and enabled the eventual release of millions of pesos in government funds.
Meanwhile, the OMB found no probable cause to charge Co, Alcantara, Estrada, and Tecsay with violating Section 3(b) of Republic Act No. 3019.
It likewise referred the perjury charge against Sally N. Santos to the Department of Justice (DOJ) for proper disposition.

articles.title: Serbia: Keeping EU, Russia in play ahead of key election
articles.summary: As Serbia heads towards an uncertain election, President Aleksandar Vucic is balancing ties with Russia and EU ambitions. But growing geopolitical tensions and pressure at home are narrowing his room…

image.caption: Aleksandar Vucic is trying to balance Serbia's ties with the EU and RussiaImage: Djordje Kojadinovic/REUTERS

blocks.text: Smoke from the wildfires still hangs over parts of Serbia, but as the flames slowly recede, another debate is taking shape in their wake — one that has less to do with firefighting and more with politics.

In early August, wildfires swept across Serbia, affecting more than 3,500 hectares (8,600 acres) in the Deliblato Sands Special Nature Reserve alone. For days, firefighters, soldiers and helicopters battled the flames.

blocks.caption: Serbia turned to Russia for help in fighting wildfires in the Deliblato Sands  Special Nature ReserveImage: Marko Dimic/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Then a Russian Ilyushin Il-76 firefighting aircraft arrived in the southern city of Nis. Serbia had turned to Moscow for help, making Russia the first foreign country it asked to provide a firefighting aircraft. Pro-government media greeted its arrival with celebratory coverage, dubbing the aircraft the "Russian beast."

"Considering that there are no firefighting aircraft of this capacity available within the European Union, the arriving Russian aircraft will significantly strengthen our capacities to fight the fires," said Luka Causic, head of the Serbian Interior Ministry's Department for Emergency Situations.
A pragmatic choice between EU, Russia — or a political signal?
The episode, however, was already being viewed through a geopolitical lens, as Serbia had sought Russian assistance before activating the EU's emergency mechanism.

When it did, the response was swift. Brussels mobilized four helicopters from its strategic rescEU reserve, based in Czechia, Romania and Slovakia, along with ground firefighting teams from Germany and Romania.

blocks.caption: Emergency services, including German firefighters, were on hand to help Serbia battle wildfiresImage: Feuerwehr Bonn/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Vucic rejected the idea that turning to Russia first was a foreign-policy decision or a sign of Serbia's political alignment with Moscow.

"As far as equipment and resources are concerned, we are a European giant. The helicopters we received from Europe to fight the fires are less capable than ours and have a lower carrying capacity than our own," Vucic said during a visit to the Deliblato Sands.
Zelenskyy in Belgrade
The wildfire episode came less than two weeks after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made his first official visit to Serbia.
The two presidents reaffirmed their support for each other's territorial integrity, which is particularly significant for Belgrade because Ukraine does not recognise Kosovo's independence.
But Vucic is also trying to keep the other side on board, says Vuk Vuksanovic, a political scientist and foreign-policy lecturer at King's College London.

Vuksanovic argues that Vucic's engagement with Zelenskyy must therefore be portrayed in Moscow not as a fundamental shift in Serbia's relationship with Russia, but as a response to Western pressure and Serbia's own interests.
"Vucic is now trying to make sure that neither the West nor Russia becomes an open opponent during the election campaign," said Vuksanovic.

"Zelenskyy was primarily received so that the ruling coalition could present itself to Europeans as a great friend of Ukraine. In the same way, Vucic is trying to present himself to the Trump administration as a great friend of Israel, primarily to ensure that neither the European Union nor the United States becomes an opponent of the ruling party during the election campaign," Vuksanovic added.
Vucic's room for maneuver is shrinking
The problem is that the room to maintain these relationships may be shrinking.
The deeper the confrontation between Russia and the West becomes, the harder it is for Serbia to remain close to both without facing pressure to choose.

The European Union increasingly expects candidate countries to align their foreign and security policies with those of the bloc. Serbia's refusal to impose sanctions on Russia remains one of the most visible obstacles to closer alignment.

But Moscow, too, has reasons not to take Belgrade's loyalty for granted, Vuksanovic said. He argues that Russia does not fully trust Vucic, even as Moscow continues to support his narrative about "color revolutions" — a reference to anti-government protests, in this case the student-led protests in Serbia that started last year, which Vucic and Russia portray as Western-backed attempts to destabilize the government.

For Vucic, however, the longer-term question of Serbia's ties with Russia can wait. The more immediate question is whether he will survive the election, tentatively scheduled for October, and remain in a position to preserve that delicate balance himself.
Edited by: Rob Mudge

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 8:41pm

The Philippine government will coordinate with Meta, the company behind Facebook, to address nihilistic violent extremism (NVE), National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag said Friday.
Matibag said the government will share information with Meta regarding possible threats of school shootings.

“As we speak now, meron na kaming mga binabato, ‘yung mga tuloy-tuloy na pumapasok sa monitoring namin na maaaring banta ng pag-uulit ng nangyari sa Tacloban at saka sa Zamboanga,” he said in an ambush interview.
(As we speak, we already have individuals being flagged, those who continue to come up in our monitoring as potential threats for a repeat of what happened in Tacloban and Zamboanga.)
“We have resolved na magkakaroon sila ng office dito kung saan ‘yung ating communication doon na papasok,” he added.
(We have resolved to have them set up an office here, where our communications will be received.)

This came after the official, the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center, representatives of the House of Representatives, the Senate, the Department of Education, the National Telecommunications Commission, among others, met with Meta in Singapore.
“Ang message dito, hindi na puwedeng magtago ‘yung mga gumagawa ng kalokohan using cyberspace,” he said.
Aside from this, Matibag said Meta will also help the government in addressing fake news and troll farms.
Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida said there is a pattern that “groomers” are inviting children who play video games to join separate chatrooms.
Matibag also previously said that the bureau has identified a “groomer” group with a supposed “tenet or bible,” wherein members are incited to commit violence. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Rwanda genocide: Dutch court sentences man to life in prison
articles.summary: The Rwandan-born Dutch national was found guilty of involvement in the massacre of around 3,000 Tutsis, including throwing a grenade into a crowd of people sheltering in a football stadium.

image.caption: Over 800,00 people are estimated to have been murdered in the 1994 Rwandan genocideImage: DW

blocks.text: A Rwandan-born Dutch national was on Friday sentenced to life imprisonment by a court in the Netherlands for his role in the 1994 Rwandan genocide.

The Hague District Court found that the 66-year-old man, identified only as Eugene N., had taken part in attacks on homes in Tutsi communities and thrown a grenade into a crowd of Tutsis sheltering in a football stadium, and convicted him of war crimes and genocide.
"The conduct of the defendant establishes a significant lack of respect for human dignity and for human life," read a statement from the court issued after the conviction.
"Only a lifelong prison sentence does justice to the immense suffering that has been inflicted on the victims and the bereaved families."
Handing down the verdict, the presiding judge said N.'s actions were committed with "genocidal intent."
Rwandan genocide: How many people died?

During the 1994 genocide in Rwanda, more than 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed in a campaign of mass murder orchestrated by Hutu extremists. Many leaders of the slaughter were tried and convicted by a United Nations war crimes tribunal that has now closed down.
N. was sentenced for his role in the massacre of around 3,000 Tutsis in Mbazi in southern Rwanda in April 1994, in which prosecutors said he was "personally involved."

"If the horrific crimes of the suspect, in which not one but an estimated 3,000 innocent people were literally slaughtered, in which the suspect personally threw a grenade into a stadium, do not deserve a life sentence, then what does?" one prosecutor asked the court.
Survivors remember Rwanda's 1994 genocide
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Defendant denies involvement in 'horrific events'
N., who the court heard had held a position of responsibility in Mbazi, denied the charges, claiming he himself had been a victim who had lost dozens of his own relatives in "those horrific events."
His lawyers had argued that their client did "everything to prevent the genocide" and had called for an acquittal on all counts.
"The case has torn his scars open again," said one defense lawyer. "He is a broken man."
But the court found that the defendant's position of responsibility made his crimes even worse since he was "held in high regard" and "must have been aware of his role" in events.
"Instead of staying on the sidelines, the defendant committed multiple severe crimes," added the court, although it did acquit N. of the charge of incitement to genocide.
Defense lawyers told the Dutch ANP news agency that they will "almost certainly appeal the charges."

N. fled to the Netherlands in 1998 and had since obtained Dutch citizenship, meaning Dutch authorities were unable to extradite him when Rwandan prosecutors issued an international warrant for his arrest back in 2014.
Dutch prosecutors opened their own investigation in 2020. They have since interviewed dozens of witnesses in Rwanda and arrested N. in 2024.
Last month, German prosecutors also announced the arrest of a man suspected of being an accomplice in the Rwandan genocide.
Rwandan genocide suspect prosecuted in Germany

articles.title: Dutch court sentences man to life over Rwanda genocide
articles.summary: The court in The Hague convicted the 66-year-old of war crimes and the crime of genocide.

blocks.text: A court in the Netherlands has sentenced a Dutch-Rwandan man to life for his involvement in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda.

The 66-year-old, named only as Eugene N, was accused, among other things, of throwing a hand grenade into a crowd of Tutsis who were seeking shelter in a stadium. He was convicted of war crimes and the crime of genocide, having acted with "genocidal intent", the judge said.
Rwanda had sought his extradition in 2014 but the authorities in the Netherlands then launched their own investigation into N, who had become a Dutch citizen.
In 100 days in April 1994, an estimated 800,000 ethnic Tutsis and politically moderate Hutus people were killed by Hutu extremists.
The court in The Hague heard N held an authoritative position in the community at the time of the massacre, overseeing around 1,000 people in Mbazi in southern Rwanda.

"The suspect was a man who was held in high regard and must have been aware of his role and the influence he had as a local administrator," the court explained, adding that he "committed multiple severe crimes".
At a football stadium, he instructed Hutus not to let any of the Tutsis escape. Trapped inside, they were pelted with stones, shot at and had hand grenades thrown at them.
Any who had survived, were killed with clubs and machetes, the court said.
Prior to the stadium massacre, N had watched on as people looted houses and set them on fire.
"Only a lifelong prison sentence does justice to the immense suffering that has been inflicted on the victims and the bereaved families," the court said.
As part of the Dutch investigation opened in 2020, more than 30 witnesses were interviewed. N was subsequently arrested in 2024.
N denied all the charges, the AFP news agency reports, alleging that he was a victim who had lost family in "those horrific events".

"The case has torn his scars open again. He is a broken man," his lawyers are quoted as saying by AFP. They had moved to seek acquittals on all accounts. N was acquitted of the incitement to genocide.
His defence team said they will "almost certainly appeal the charges", according to local news agency ANP.

articles.title: 100-machine dialysis center to offer free treatment in Manila
articles.summary: A 100-machine dialysis and rehabilitation center that will offer free treatment to qualified Manila residents will be established at the Gat Andres Bonifacio Memorial Medical Center (GABMMC) in…

blocks.text: (CONTRIBUTED PHOTO)

A 100-machine dialysis and rehabilitation center that will offer free treatment to qualified Manila residents will be established at the Gat Andres Bonifacio Memorial Medical Center (GABMMC) in Tondo.

The Manila City government and Prime Dialysis Center Inc. (PDCI) broke ground for the Flora V. Valisno De Siojo Dialysis Center along Delpan Street on Monday, Aug. 24, for the project expected to become one of the country's largest free dialysis facilities.
Under an agreement signed on Aug. 13, PDCI will rehabilitate, renovate, and equip the facility and participate in its operation as the private-sector partner of the City Government of Manila.

The company wants to replicate the success stories in the 35 dialysis centers it operats nationwide, including facilities in underserved areas such as Gen. Tinio in Nueva Ecija, Mabinay in Negros Oriental and Alicia in Isabela, where some patients once had to travel for hours or more than 100 kilometers to receive dialysis
The center will primarily serve qualified patients from Manila’s First District and nearby communities.
Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno” Domagoso said the project forms part of the city government’s efforts to modernize and equip its public healthcare facilities.

“We are really trying to modernize, equip, and make it a more delightful facility. Hindi ’yung mema lang—may magawa lang o may masabi lang (Not just for show or simply to say that we did something). We always wanted the best for our people,” Domagoso said.
The project will complement PhilHealth’s coverage of 156 dialysis sessions, which allows qualified patients to undergo treatment three times a week.
“Dialysis access should be available to every Filipino patient,” said PDCI Chief Executive Officer Dr. Gjay Ordinal, a nephrologist who entered the dialysis industry in 2003.

He said the project reflects the company's more than two decades of efforts to address two major barriers to kidney care—the high cost of treatment and the distance patients often have to travel to reach dialysis centers.

"More than twenty years ago, I started in this industry as a young nephrologist with a huge frustration: too many of my patients could not survive," Ordinal said, noting that many patients previously struggled with the cost of treatment and the lack of accessible dialysis facilities.

"This facility will not just be a building. It will be a lifeline for hundreds of patients from District 1 and beyond who need dialysis simply to see another day, and a place of healing and rehabilitation for those working their way back to strength,” he added.

articles.title: Influential humanists: These are the winners of the Goethe Medal 2026
articles.summary: The prestigious German cultural award recognizes the artistic work and commitment to cultural dialogue of Arvo Pärt, Anita Raja and Prodromos Tsinikoris.

image.caption: Agents of intercultural dialogue: documentary theater director Prodromos Tsinikoris, composer Arvo Pärt and translator Anita RajaImage: DW/picture alliance/Imago

blocks.text: Estonian classical music composer Arvo Pärt, Italian literary translator Anita Raja and Greek theater director and actor Prodromos Tsinikoris are the three recipients of the 2026 Goethe Medal, an annual award that honors international public figures who contribute to creating cultural bridges between Germany and partner countries.
The annual award, presented this year on August 28 in Weimar, is one of the most prestigious awards in Germany for international cultural work.
So what connects these three personalities to Germany's culture?
A prolific German exile: Estonian composer Arvo Pärt

Considered one of the most influential figures in contemporary classical music since the 1960s, the Estonian composer is renowned for his minimalist, contemplative compositional technique called "tintinnabula."
With his iconic works including "Für Alina" (1976), "Fratres" (1977), "Tabula rasa" (1977) and "Spiegel im Spiegel" (1978), Pärt is one of the most performed living composers in the world.

In 1980, the composer was forced to leave his home country, and his works were banned in the Soviet Union. After leaving then Soviet Estonia, Pärt settled in West Berlin with his family. He lived in Germany for nearly three decades.

"Germany plays such an important part in my father's work," Michael Pärt told DW. The composer's son added that his renowned father found creative freedom through his collaborations with different German conductors and musicians. He was also inspired to compose works to German texts.
Goethe Medal 2026 for Arvo Pärt
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Pärt's minimalist and spiritual works found a broad audience in the West thanks to the recordings of Manfred Eicher, founder of the Munich-based record label ECM.
After Estonia gained independence in 1991, Pärt reestablished contacts with his home country and returned there permanently in 2010.

The composer, who turned 90 in September 2025, now lives in the Estonian village of Laulasmaa, where the Arvo Pärt Centre opened in 2018. It is directed by his son, Michael Pärt, who will be traveling to Weimar to pick up the award on behalf of his father.
One of the most significant translators from German into Italian: Anita Raja
Born in Naples in 1953 to an Italian father and a German mother, Anita Raja studied literature in Rome, where she still lives.
Specialized in the translation of modern German-language authors, Raja introduced East German author Christa Wolf to Italian readers with her translation of "Cassandra" in the early 1980s.

"Anita Raja's translation is a translation from woman to woman. It's very empathetic, very powerful. It shows that there really was a surprisingly magical connection between the author and the translator," noted renowned Italian actor Sonia Bergamasco at a recent event marking the release of a new edition of the novel.
Wolf became a widely celebrated author in Italy thanks to this first translation, and Raja then went on to translate many more of Wolf's novels.
Goethe Medal 2026 for Anita Raja
She has also translated the works of other major German-language writers, including Georg Büchner, Franz Kafka and Ingeborg Bachmann.

All while translating literature, Raja also worked full-time as a librarian in Rome. She became the founding director of the Biblioteca Europea in Rome in 2005, heading it for more than 10 years. She turned the library into a model project focusing on the promotion of European cultures, languages and international cooperation.
Prodromos Tsinikoris: Documentary theater as a bridge between cultures
Born in the West German city of Wuppertal in 1981 as the son of Greek labor migrants, Prodromos Tsinikoris is one of the leading voices in contemporary Greek and European theater.
As a theater director, actor and dramaturg, he creates documentary productions exploring the themes of migration, social inequality and historical perspectives.
Goethe Medal 2026 for Prodromos Tsinikoris
His audio walk "In the middle of the street" centers on homeless people during Greece's financial crisis.

The documentary theater production "Clean City," co-created with Anestis Azas, focuses on the lives of migrant cleaners, juxtaposing their personal testimonies with the rhetoric of neo-fascist movements who want to "clean" Greece of its foreigners and refugees.
In the play "96%" Tsinikoris deals with the Holocaust of the Jews of Thessaloniki and the looting of their property during the Nazi occupation.

From 2015 to 2020, Tsinikoris directed the Experimental Stage at the National Theater in Athens. Today, he is co-curator of the International Forest Festival in Thessaloniki and teaches at the National Theater's directing school in Athens.

Many of Tsinikoris' plays have been developed and presented in Germany. His work has also circulated broadly across Europe, particularly through documentary theater festivals and major public theaters.
Edited by: Brenda Haas

articles.title: Dasmariñas City casts vote for new congressman
articles.summary: Here is what to expect during the special election on August 29. Five candidates are vying for the congressional seat vacated by the expelled Kiko Barzaga.

blocks.text: CAVITE, Philippines – Voters in Dasmariñas City will choose on Saturday, August 29, who their congressional representative will be, replacing the expelled Kiko Barzaga.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has declared August 29 a special non-working day in Dasmariñas via Proclamation No. 1369 to enable voters to participate in the special election.
The first-class city, which comprises the 4th District of Cavite, has 447,387 registered voters from 75 barangays.
Five candidates are vying for the congressional seat:

items: Mayor Jenny Barzaga, mother of Kiko and a former congresswoman herself
Marvin Dupal-ag
Former councilor Jesse Frani, who gave Kiko a close fight in 2025
Former vice mayor Rex Mangubat
Leysander Aguilar Ordenes

blocks.text: Kiko Barzaga was expelled by the House of Representatives last June 2 for disorderly behavior, conduct unbecoming of a member, and violations of the House’s Code of Conduct. He is the second lawmaker in Philippine history to face such a penalty.

He was previously suspended for repeatedly interrupting House sessions, mocking chamber leaders like then-speaker Martin Romualdez, and making slanderous remarks while broadcasting plenary sessions on the budget without permission.

He continued with his disruptive behavior, leading the House ethics committee to conclude that “another penalty of suspension will not likely deter the improper behavior that reflects negatively on the House.”

items: [Tech Thoughts] Kiko Barzaga’s House expulsion is just about right
Kiko Barzaga’s playbook: When shitposting becomes a political tool
LIST: The social media posts that got Kiko Barzaga in trouble

blocks.text: Jenny Barzaga is the current mayor of Dasmariñas, and is on her last term. When her husband, the dynasty patriarch Elpidio, was stil alive, the two of them traded posts as mayor and district representative whenever they reached their term limits.

If and when she wins as congresswoman, the mayor’s post she will vacate will be assumed by the vice mayor, who is her other son, Elpidio Barzaga III. For the special election, Jenny got the endorsement of Cavite Governor Abeng Remulla and Vice Governor Ram Revilla.
Frani, a former councilor, challenged Kiko Barzaga in the congressional race in 2025, and lost by only around 15,000 votes — a historically narrow margin for a Barzaga candidate.

Frani specifically campaigned on working for a retarded basin for the city, expansion and improvement of the emergency room of the Pagamutan ng Dasmariñas, and the establishment of a state university.

Mangubat is the immediate former vice mayor of Dasmariñas. His three consecutive terms ended in 2025. In an interview with Rappler, he urged voters to choose their candidate wisely because that’s the only way to address the problems of the city and improve the residents’ lives.
The special election will use the manual voting process in all 43 voting centers, with 1,308 clustered precincts.
Early voting hours, from 5 am to 7 am, will be exclusively for senior citizens, persons with disability (PWDs), and pregnant voters.
Regular voting hours will be from 7 am to 3 pm. There will still be a special lane for senior citizens, PWDs, and pregnant voters during the regular voting window.
The local police have set up checkpoints around the city, while implementing a gun ban until September 13.
Buying, selling, and drinking of alcoholic beverages is also prohibited starting Friday, August 28, until election day.
“Hopefully, we can proclaim the winner on Sunday, August 30,” Commission on Elections Chairman George Garcia said. – Rappler.com
Follow updates on the Dasmariñas election in the Philippine Politics channel on the Rappler app.

articles.title: DOH: Wading through floodwaters can cause leptospirosis even without wounds
articles.summary: The Department of Health (DOH) on Wednesday urged the public to seek medical advice after wading through floodwaters, regardless of whether they have open wounds.

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 8:05pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
The Department of Health (DOH) on Wednesday urged the public to seek medical advice after wading through floodwaters, regardless of whether they have open wounds.
The country has recorded 5,486 leptospirosis cases from January to August 26, 2026, according to DOH Undersecretary Gloria Balboa.
“May sugat man o wala, at may sintomas man o wala, ay dapat po na pumunta na sa pinakamalapit na health center para maagapan at mabigyan ng tamang advice ng ating mga health workers,” Balboa said.
(Whether you have a wound or not, whether or not you have symptoms, you should go to the nearest health center to seek treatment early and be given the right advice by our health workers.)

Balboa explained that there are three different risk levels. A person is low-risk if he wades through a flood but does not have any cuts, and a person is at moderate risk if he wades through a flood with an open wound.
A high-risk person is someone who repeatedly wades through floods. Balboa said that this was why most leptospirosis cases affect adults—they were likely working.
National Kidney and Transplant Institute (NKTI) Executive Director Dante Dator said that there are preventive measures.

“Ang sagot ko po sa tanong na kapag nalusong, prophylaxis po, automatic po yun, kahit wala kayo naramdaman. Mas simple po yung prophylaxis or preventive kaysa sa maghintay ka ng sintomas,” Dator said,
(My answer is when someone wades, it is prophylaxis, automatically, even if you do not feel anything. Prophylaxis is easier and it is preventive, rather than waiting for symptoms.)
"Once you have symptoms, you are already sick and you might have to get confined," Dator said.
Prophylaxis is medication taken to prevent a disease. For leptospirosis, this is doxycycline. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: South Korea leans toward military conscription for women
articles.summary: Facing a population decline, fewer potential service members and calls for social equality to be extended to national military service, Korea is inching closer to breaking the taboo on women on the…

image.caption: South Korea's armed forces are experiencing significant personnel shortagesImage: Xinhua/IMAGO

blocks.text: Nearly 60% of South Koreans are now in favor of young women serving mandatory military service alongside their male counterparts, according to a recent survey, representing a significant shift in the long-held taboo against women being obliged to defend the nation.
Thousands of women already serve in the South Korean armed forces on a voluntary basis, but the debate over mandatory service has always been delicate.

Now, for a series of reasons that include a falling birth rate and shrinking number of recruits as well as an insistence that social equality means that women should also serve, the issue has re-emerged ahead of a reform of the national defense plan scheduled to be released this autumn.
Yet, there are still those who insist women should be kept away from the front lines and, instead, that South Korea should invest more in drones and other advanced technologies.
"South Korea's male-centered conscription system has long been closely connected to traditional gender roles," said Hyobin Lee, a professor at Sogang University in Seoul.

"Men were generally expected to protect the country and the family and to fight in wartime, while women were expected to take primary responsibility for childbirth, childcare and the household," she told DW.
A second factor is the intensifying debate about gender equality, a debate in large part driven by young men, she said.
Warfare moves beyond the physical
"South Korean men generally perform their military service in their early 20s, which interrupts their education, employment or early career development," Lee said.
"At the same time, gender equality has become an increasingly important social value, and women's opportunities in education and employment have expanded."

"As a result, some younger men ask a very simple question: If society expects equality in rights and opportunities, why does one of the country's most significant civic obligations — military service — still fall only on men?"
South Korea proposes talks to officially end war with North
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Another contributing factor is the change in the nature of the military itself, with a shift away from physically demanding combat roles that were perceived as being more suited to men and the emergence of a national defense more heavily reliant on technology.
This includes unmanned systems, cyber capabilities, information and communications technology and others that do not require physical strength.
What does the study show?

According to the study, carried out by the Reform Institute, the policy research arm of the conservative-leaning Reform Party, and published on August 20, almost 60% of the respondents were in favor of changing the law to require women to undergo national service. Just 34% were opposed to the idea.
Nearly 65% of men were in favor — a figure that rose to 71.7% among men in their 20s and 30s — with 54.5% of women across all age groups similarly supportive.

At present, all able-bodied men are required to complete a minimum of 18 months and up to 21 months of service and can be called back into service in the event of a national emergency, such as war breaking out on the tense Korean Peninsula.
The latest figures highlight, however, personnel shortages that have affected South Korea's armed forces.

According to the Defense Ministry, around 332,000 men were eligible to perform mandatory military service in 2019. That number fell to 257,000 men in 2022 and is forecast to shrink to just 120,000 men in 2043.

While Hyobin Lee is strongly in favor of equality throughout South Korean society, she fears that obliging women to serve the same military terms as men may turn out to be a negative because so many other elements in society still lag.
Women's traditional responsibilities remain unchanged
"Women in South Korea still bear a much greater share of the responsibilities associated with pregnancy, childbirth and childcare," she underlined.

"Having a child can still lead to career interruption or withdrawal from the labor market, and women's responsibilities for caregiving have not declined to the same extent that their participation in education and employment has increased," Lee added.
Korean 'comfort women' memorial angers Japan
"If women were also required to complete military service, the cumulative burden across their life course could become even greater," she pointed out.
"In a country that is already experiencing an extremely low birth rate, it is also possible that this additional compulsory obligation could further delay or discourage marriage and childbirth."
Lee comes from a family with a strong military background, with a grandfather an admiral in the navy and her father serving in the same branch of the military.
But she would have had reservations in completing mandatory service herself.
"If someone chooses a military career, that is completely different from compulsory service," she said.

"Eighteen months in your 20s is a very significant period in a person's life. It is a time when people are studying, beginning their careers, and making important personal choices. Having to put all of that on hold because the state requires it is a substantial burden," she said.
"Personally, I would have found it extremely difficult to give up 18 months of my younger years in that way."

Song Young-Chae, a Seoul-based academic and human rights activist, completed two years in the infantry as a younger man, when periods of service were longer. He is opposed to mandatory service for women.
"The defense of the nation is traditionally the responsibility of men, and I do not believe that there is such an urgent need to conscript women into front-line service," he told DW.
Need to invest in modern technology

"I served along the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) with North Korea, and it was a hard posting," he added. "I believe that we should be investing far more in drones, robots and other advanced military technologies to protect our borders."
How China's rise is shaping Trump's strategy in Asia

The South Korean government set up a task force in 2025 to revise the nation's basic defense plan, with troop modernization and an overhaul of the conscription system — introduced in the 1950s — high on the agenda.

In an interview with the Yonhap News Agency on August 9, Military Manpower Commissioner Hong So-young admitted that the nation faces a "demographic cliff" and that reforms are urgently required. Those include potentially reducing the number of people exempt from service and requiring foreign-born people who have taken South Korean nationality to also serve.
Hong made no comment about mandatory service for Korean women, but said the system needs a "fundamental" overhaul.
Edited by: Shamil Shams

blocks.text: A congressman from north Luzon is prodding the House Committee on Local Government to tell local government units (LGUs) to explore “rescue buys” of farmers’ crops in a bid to prevent produce dumping.
This, as Abra lone district Rep. JB Bernos cited circulating reports of dumping of crops, with truckloads of carrots and cabbage reportedly being dumped by the roadside in Tublay, Benguet.
The cause according to farmers? An oversupply of the crops, coupled with the lack of buyers.

“Bilang frontliner at pinakamalapit na unit ng pamahalaan sa komunidad, maganda siguro kung tayo na rin ang manguna sa pagsalba sa ating mga magsasaka para hindi masayang ang pinagpaguran nila,” Bernos said.
(As frontliners and the closest unit of government to the community, it would be good if we also take the lead in helping save our farmers so that their hard work does not go to waste.)
According to Bernos, the crops could be purchased and then be distributed to struggling families so they may have food to eat.
Bernos said that some LGUs have already done such an initiative, particularly in attempts to save both crops and animal produce during typhoons and other disasters.
“May mga model LGUs na tayo na bumibili ng mga produkto ng ating mga magsasaka’t mangingisda at ipinamimigay ito lalo na sa panahon ng sakuna,” he said.
(There are already model LGUs that buy the products of our farmers and fisherfolk and distribute them, especially during times of calamity.)
He also backed Department of Education (DepEd) Secretary Sonny Angara’s proposal to use surplus vegetables in the government’s expanded school feeding program.
Angara recently said the DepEd was exploring ways to use surplus fresh vegetables in school feeding programs, which now reaches 4.6 million beneficiaries, including Kindergarten and Grade 1 learners.

articles.title: India's citizen-led school audits test limits of activism
articles.summary: The student-led "Cockroach" movement is taking its campaign for accountability to government schools, but the activists' methods are encountering growing resistance from authorities.

image.caption: The CJP has said many government schools are in need of improvement Image: Madhan Kumar/DW

blocks.text: The Indian activist movement dubbing itself the "Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)" shot to national prominence in May by leading weeks-long protests over a scandal involving highly competitive entrance exams.
The student-led campaign put the government under intense political pressure and ended with the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July.
Now, the CJP is taking aim at India's government schools, organizing volunteer visits to classrooms, documenting conditions and demanding accountability for problems.

Launched on August 15, Independence Day in India, the campaign asks parents, students and volunteers to inspect schools and record basic facilities including toilets, drinking water, electricity, classroom furniture and school buildings. The CJP has said the findings will be used to pressure authorities to make improvements.
The initial target is to audit 100 rural government schools over two months. It has also proposed giving recognition to village leaders who improve their schools.

Unlike the first campaign, which was based on street protests, the school audits require a more sustained form of local activism. Volunteers are expected to work consistently at the local level, document conditions and follow up with officials, parents and communities.

blocks.caption: Students celebrated in New Delhi after the resignation of India's education minister in JulyImage: Raj K Raj/Hindustan Times/Sipa USA/picture alliance

blocks.text: The organization is dealing with different layers of the Indian administration. Responsibility for government schools is divided between state governments, local administrations and elected village bodies. The CJP is therefore set to tackle different rules and political interests across the country.
India has over a million government schools, according to Education Ministry data. They make up nearly 70% of all schools in the country but serve less than half of its 247 million schoolchildren.
CJP: 'We are not afraid'
That scale has given CJP a vast field for its campaign. But it has also brought a new set of challenges.
The authorities are raising questions regarding rules and locations for the CJP scrutiny, as well as safeguards when children are present.
The response is already varying from state to state. Some authorities have ordered their own inspections, while others have restricted access or taken police action against CJP volunteers.
Authorities in Maharashtra and Rajasthan states have objected to school visits carried out without permission.
In one case, a complaint by school authorities resulted in police action against CJP members after they entered the premises to conduct an audit.

In Rajasthan, restrictions have been imposed on outsiders entering government schools, as well as on filming, interviews and other forms of documentation. CJP volunteers in Rajasthan have also said they were attacked while inspecting a school.
"We are not afraid. We are seeking accountability from the government," said CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka.
Officials say schools are not open spaces

In the state of Uttar Pradesh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has ordered officials to conduct on-the-spot checks of school facilities and directed police to register cases over what he called misleading videos about schools and colleges.
India's 'Cockroach' protesters claim online censorship
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
The CJP has said such measures undermine public scrutiny. Authorities have said schools are not open spaces for unauthorized inspections, particularly when children are present.
Vinita Gursahani Singh, managing trustee of We, The People campaign, which works on citizen empowerment, said the limits are set by law.

"Under the Right to Information Act, any citizen can inspect schools but you need to submit an application. And that makes sense as there has to be consideration for students and teaching," Singh told DW.
"All public scrutiny is legitimate. It is our job to scrutinize. But the scrutiny has to follow process. It has to be even-handed. What applies to one citizen must apply to all," she said.
Can activists serve as inspectors?
The CJP maintains government schools are publicly funded institutions and citizens have a legitimate right to ask how they are functioning.
Its volunteers use standardized audit forms to record conditions and send their findings to the CJP, which has said it will use the material to press local administrations to respond.

But critics question whether citizen activists can assume the role of inspectors. There are concerns about whether volunteers have the expertise to assess safety or infrastructure problems and how allegations posted on social media are verified.
Mohandas Pai, an education advocate, supports CJP's focus on government schools but disagrees with its methods.
"I like young people taking interest in school education. It's a broken system, and we need reforms," Pai told DW.
But he objected to large groups entering schools and questioning headmasters and children.
"You can't just barge into a school just because you think you are entitled to do it," Pai said, stressing that "children have to have a safe, secure environment."
India's elementary school helping students escape poverty
Pai said the CJP should instead send small teams with permission, collect systematic data, publish regular reports and use the evidence to pressure governments.
CJP spokesperson Saurav Das rejected the argument that the campaign should rely on conventional channels, saying such approaches have failed to bring meaningful change.
Responding to Pai on X, he challenged him to join the next school visit and show the volunteers how it should be done.
Questions of student privacy
The audit campaign has also raised questions about privacy, consent and disruption of teaching when volunteers enter schools, film inside classrooms or question students.
However, Kavita Srivastava, president of the People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) Rajasthan, opposes restrictions on outsiders entering schools and taking photos and videos in her state.

"Activists were visiting government schools to document their condition and demand accountability. Protecting children's privacy should not be used to prevent legitimate public scrutiny of government schools," Srivastava told DW.
A new role for the CJP
Activist Amrita Johri said the CJP's first campaign tapped into a longstanding accountability gap in India's examination system, which cost millions of young people time and money.
"The demand for accountability had popular resonance because there was no real response from the government," Johri told DW.
She backed the school audit campaign, saying public scrutiny should be welcomed.

"Public audits are an integral part of citizens' right to information and should be welcomed as an opportunity to fix accountability," she said. Johri added that the CJP needs to train volunteers, document problems and follow up with authorities to make the campaign effective.

articles.title: DA soft-launches livestock data systems for wider 2027 rollout
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture (DA) on Friday announced it has soft-launched two digital systems for livestock data ahead of its rollout next year as part of efforts to modernize the Philippine animal…

blocks.text: The Department of Agriculture (DA) on Friday announced it has soft-launched two digital systems for livestock data ahead of their rollout next year as part of efforts to modernize the Philippine animal industry.

In a news release, the DA said the Animal Management Information System (AMIS) and Livestock Registry System (LRS), developed under Republic Act No. 12308 or the Animal Industry Development and Competitiveness Act, will initially integrate administrative data from four major livestock agencies.

The soft launching of AMIS and LRS brought together the Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI), Philippine Carabao Center (PCC), National Dairy Authority (NDA), and National Meat Inspection Service (NMIS), laying the foundation for wider data integration ahead of a more comprehensive launch targeted for 2027.
“Better information means better decisions. Better coordination means faster response,” said Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr.
Other Stories
“If we know what animals we have, where they are, and what is happening in the field, we can detect problems earlier, respond faster, improve productivity, and protect livelihoods,” added Tiu Laurel.
The DA said the AMIS, mandated under Section 13 of RA 12308, will serve as the central repository for animal industry information from the municipal to national levels.

It will bring together data on animal production and inventory, health and vaccination, facilities, supply and demand, trade, feeds, prices, research and technologies, diseases, and government programs.

The system will process, validate, and analyze the information to generate reports, forecasts, maps, and other decision-support tools for government, farmers, livestock producers, researchers, and policymakers.
For an industry where a disease outbreak can move faster than paperwork, having timely information could prove critical, according to the DA.
The LRS, meanwhile, will serve as the master list of eligible beneficiaries of the Animal Competitiveness Enhancement Fund, or AnCEF, under Section 17 of RA 12038.
The DA said the development of LRS will involve consultations with farmers’ organizations, cooperatives, and local government units.
BAI will administer the systems, while the livestock agencies will contribute data, technical expertise, and validation based on their respective mandates, it said.
The DA said that the soft launch would be an initial demonstration of the systems’ capabilities and a foundation for broader implementation.
It said the succeeding phase will expand data coverage and participation to other DA offices, government agencies, LGUs, research institutions, and industry stakeholders.
It will also focus on interoperability, data standardization, cybersecurity, and stronger data governance.
The DA said broader 2027 rollout of the two systems is expected to feature expanded datasets, wider agency participation, and enhanced analytics and decision-support capabilities.

The Agriculture Department said the AMIS and LRS would help the government monitor production and animal health more effectively, strengthen disease response and food safety, target programs and resources better, and make policy decisions based on reliable information.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: People from over 30 countries missing after Nepal, China floods
articles.summary: Catastrophic flash floods in a border area of China and Nepal have killed at least 472 people and left more than 1,500 people missing as of Friday morning. Hundreds were foreigners in the area to…

blocks.caption: Damaged houses stand precariously near the swollen, debris-choked banks of the Trishuli River after flash floods in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026. — Photo by Associated Press

blocks.text: Catastrophic flash floods in a border area of China and Nepal have killed at least 472 people and left more than 1,500 people missing as of Friday morning. Hundreds were foreigners in the area to work, take guided treks or make a pilgrimage to a sacred Hindu site.

Thousands have been rescued, with some of the injured taken to hospitals in Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu. The number of missing from Wednesday’s disaster may vary because of progress in the ongoing rescue efforts and differences in how data was collected and verified among agencies.
A look at how multiple countries have been affected:
Nepal

Nepal’s disaster management authority said Friday morning the death toll rose to 469, with 977 people missing. The authority said 3,253 people have been rescued by helicopter, and more than 150 of the injured were taken to hospitals in Kathmandu and the districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading.

Local reports cited the National Emergency Operation Center as saying Thursday the missing included 113 Nepali tourists, 85 security personnel from the army and police as well as 161 residents from the Rasuwa district and one from the Nuwakot district.
China

State media reported Thursday at least three people died and 558 were missing in Gyirong County, Tibet. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that 260 of the 558 missing people were foreigners. In addition, nearly 100 Chinese citizens were missing on the Nepal side, China’s foreign ministry said.
India

India’s External Affairs Ministry said 288 Indian nationals remain uncontactable. They included 73 people who were working on a power project. Nepal officials have said many Indian tourists were on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus.
United States
The U.S. State Department said 90 Americans were unaccounted for in China and Nepal. It said it was not aware of any U.S. deaths. Three Americans have been rescued.
Malaysia
The board said 51 Malaysians were missing.
Ukraine

Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry said that 55 Ukrainians are missing. The number includes two tourist groups of 47 and seven people, in addition to one Ukrainian woman traveling with a foreign tour group, the ministry said.
Australia
The Australian government said 39 Australians were missing.
Britain
The board said 33 of the missing were from Britain.
Canada
Nepal’s tourism board said 25 of the missing were from Canada.
South Korea
South Korean government officials said nine citizens working on building a hydropower plant in Nepal were missing.
Singapore
Eight Singaporeans were missing, according to Nepal tourism board.
Germany
Nepal’s tourism board said eight tourists from Germany were missing.
Russia
The Russian Embassy in Nepal said eight of its citizens were missing.
South Africa
The board said six South Africans were missing.
Latvia
The board said six tourists from Latvia were missing.
Japan
Japanese media said the five Japanese tourists missing are a couple and their children.
New Zealand
Five people from New Zealand were missing, said Nepal’s tourism board.
France
The board said four French citizens were missing.
Belgium
The board said three from Belgium were missing.
Spain
The board said three visitors from Spain were missing.

articles.title: Norway’s crown prince becomes King Haakon VIII after his father’s death
articles.summary: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Norway has a new king, whose tasks will include stabilizing the Scandinavian country’s monarchy and boosting the royal family’s popularity after his wife’s…

blocks.caption: Norwegian Crown Prince Haakon looks on during a tour at the Amazon Spheres, Wednesday, April 17, 2024, in Seattle. — File photo by Associated Press

blocks.text: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Norway has a new king, whose tasks will include stabilizing the Scandinavian country’s monarchy and boosting the royal family’s popularity after his wife’s past contacts with deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his stepson’s rape conviction.
Crown Prince Haakon, 53, became King Haakon VIII when his father, Harald V, died Friday. Haakon’s oldest child now becomes Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra and the heir to the throne.
Haakon knows the ropes. As his father aged and his health began to fail in recent years, the prince stepped in as the country’s regent on several occasions.

Norway’s monarchy has old roots, tracing its origins to King Harald Fairhair in the ninth century. When Norway regained its independence in 1905, three-quarters of voters in a national plebiscite approved restoring the monarchy. Today, the role is largely symbolic as the power lies with an elected parliament, but the country’s royal family retains celebrity and a role in promoting the wealthy nation around the world.

Haakon is the younger child of Harald, born two years after his sister, Princess Märtha Louise. As the oldest male, however, he became heir to the throne when his grandfather, King Olav, died in 1991. The Norwegian Constitution was altered in 1990 to allow future firstborns — regardless of gender — to take precedence in the line of succession. However, it was not applied retroactively.
Haakon said in a 1998 book that as a child he dreamed of owning a toy shop, but he soon realized that his path was already paved and one day he would become king.

He holds a bachelor’s degree in political science from the University of California at Berkeley and a master’s degree in development studies from the London School of Economics and Political Science, with a specialization in international trade and Africa. In 1995, he graduated from the Royal Norwegian Naval Academy, and he also completed the Foreign Ministry’s trainee program for diplomats.

An avid surfer, skier and sportsman, he told Norwegian broadcaster NRK that if he hadn’t been a royal, he would have been a surfer. A music lover — he likes rock and rap — he attended festivals across Europe as a youth.
Haakon sought the king’s permission to marry

When Haakon met Mette-Marit Tjessem Høiby — a single mother whose son’s father had been sentenced to prison for cocaine possession — at a popular music festival in Norway in 1999, he knew it was going to be an uphill battle, especially since she also had been seen at parties where illegal drugs were used.
The country was divided. Some cheered for love, others were skeptical. The Norwegian newspaper VG wrote in 2000 that Haakon “lives closer to the people than any other heir to the throne before him.”
In a May 2000 interview with NRK, Haakon said that in the early 1990s, “a youth culture emerged in Oslo” and he acknowledged that Mette-Marit was “an active part of this environment at the time.”
“It is clear that there is relatively extravagant partying there,” Haakon said.

Nevertheless, he won permission from his father, who had also married a commoner, to wed Mette-Marit. And despite her background, the Norwegian people found much to like about this statuesque blond woman with striking eyes and a ready smile, a down-to-earth manner and an undisguised love for Haakon.

They wed in August 2001 at the Oslo Cathedral. The couple’s popularity soared thanks to a carefully cultivated blend of the common touch and the glamor and grace demanded of royalty. They were constantly on the covers of gossip magazines, yet tried to live relatively normal and private family lives.
They have two children, Ingrid Alexandra and Prince Sverre Magnus. Haakon also became the stepfather of Mette-Marit’s son, Marius Borg Høiby, who has no royal title.
Royal family’s reputation took a hit from Høiby’s trial

In June, Høiby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of rape. He was found guilty of two of the four rape charges he was facing and acquitted of the other two. He was also convicted of assault and abuse in a close relationship. Høiby’s lawyers said he will appeal the convictions.

The trial unfolded amid renewed scrutiny of the royal family following disclosures about Mette-Marit’s past contacts with Jeffrey Epstein, the deceased sex offender. She has publicly apologized for the association and said she exercised poor judgment in maintaining contact with him. She isn’t accused of any wrongdoing.
In a television interview in March, she said she was manipulated and deceived by Epstein and felt unsafe during a 2013 encounter with him at his Palm Beach, Florida, mansion.

In 2018, the royal palace announced that Mette-Marit had been diagnosed with a rare form of chronic pulmonary fibrosis, meaning she sometimes must take a break from her official duties. The incurable condition made breathing increasingly difficult, she had a dry cough and fatigue, weight loss and loss of appetite. She received a lung transplant in June.

In connection with the couple’s 50th birthdays in 2023, NRK interviewed Haakon and aired an old video of him playing guitar, with Ingrid Alexandra and Mette-Marit singing, and another one where he and his children mimic the moves of a Norwegian rapper. He watched the clips and burst into laughter, saying that they showed that “I am all in.”

One task for the new king will be to shore up popular support for the royal family. While a majority of people still support it, the proportion has declined in recent years and took a battering this year as Høiby’s trial played out. Critics of Haakon’s sister, Märtha Louise, who has written books in which she claimed to have contact with angels, also blame her for the family’s reputational troubles.

Märtha Louise, who was previously married for 14 years, in 2024 wed Durek Verrett, an American who describes himself as a shaman and a healer on his website. In 2022, she announced that she would no longer officially represent the Norwegian royal house, following “many questions relating to me and my fiancé’s role.”

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Friday said it is awaiting confirmation from Nepali authorities on a Filipino national reported missing after a glacial collapse triggered a massive debris flow, sending water, mud, rock and ice surging through communities along the Nepal-Tibet border. on Wednesday.

DFA spokesperson Analyn Ratonel said the Philippine Embassy in New Delhi and the Philippine Honorary Consulate General in Kathmandu are coordinating with local authorities and are ready to assist Filipinos affected by the disaster.
“They are awaiting confirmation from Nepali authorities on a Filipino national who is reported missing,” Ratonel said in a message to reporters.
The reported missing Filipino appeared in a preliminary record released by the Nepal Tourism Board, which listed one Filipino among travelers unaccounted for in the affected areas.
The Philippine government has yet to independently confirm the report.
Ratonel also said the DFA had forwarded to the concerned office information provided by Chiara Manalo about her brother, Filipino doctor Juan Carlos Manalo.
The DFA has not confirmed that Manalo is the missing Filipino listed in the preliminary record.
Chiara Manalo appealed for help locating her brother, saying he had been out of contact since the disaster struck.
In a Facebook post Friday, she said the family last heard from Manalo at 1:21 p.m. Philippine time on Tuesday.
She said Manalo was traveling with the Isha Sadghuru group on a Kailashyatra tour. The group’s last known location, according to the family, was at the Immigration Office in Gyirong.
“Please help us look for my brother,” Chiara Manalo said.

The family asked anyone with information about Manalo or members of the group to contact them. It also appealed for help in connecting them with agencies that could coordinate with Nepali authorities and ongoing search operations.

articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The family of Filipino doctor Juan Carlos Manalo has appealed for help locating him after losing contact with him following flash floods near the Nepal-Tibet border. Manalo’s…

blocks.caption: Damaged houses stand precariously near the swollen, debris-choked banks of the Trishuli River after flash floods in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Niranjan Shrestha)

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The family of Filipino doctor Juan Carlos Manalo has appealed for help locating him after losing contact with him following flash floods near the Nepal-Tibet border.
Manalo’s sister, Chiara Manalo, said on Friday that the family had not heard from him since Tuesday, a day before the disaster struck the area.
In a Facebook post, Chiara said the family’s last contact with Manalo was at 1:21 p.m. Philippine time on Tuesday or 11:06 a.m. Nepal time.
She said Manalo was traveling with the Isha Sadghuru group on a Kailashyatra tour. The group’s last known location was at the Immigration Office in Gyirong, according to the family.
“Please help us look for my brother,” Chiara said.

The family appealed to anyone with information about Manalo or members of the group to contact them. It also asked for help connecting with agencies that could coordinate with Nepali authorities and assist in search operations.
“Receiving and seeing the news about the catastrophe has been very difficult for us. We humbly ask to include him in your prayers, that he may return to us safely soon,” the family said.

The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said Friday that the Philippine Embassy in New Delhi and the Philippine Honorary Consulate General in Kathmandu were coordinating with local authorities and were ready to assist Filipinos affected by the disaster.
DFA spokesperson Analyn Ratonel said the agency was awaiting confirmation from Nepali authorities on a Filipino national who was reported missing.
Ratonel also said the DFA had forwarded to the concerned office information provided by Chiara about her brother.

The reported missing Filipino appeared in a preliminary record released by the Nepal Tourism Board, which listed one Filipino among travelers unaccounted for in the affected areas. The Philippine government has yet to independently confirm the report.
The disaster struck Wednesday after a glacial collapse triggered a massive debris flow, sending water, mud, rock and ice through communities along the Nepal-Tibet border.
The DFA has not confirmed that Manalo is the Filipino listed in the preliminary Nepal Tourism Board record.
