articles.title: Nova Scotians wait over 500 ‘painful’ days for surgery consultations
articles.summary: When the consultation and surgery wait times are combined, the total waits for hip and knee replacements in Nova Scotia are longer than they were a decade ago. In 2015, Nova Scotians could expect a…

image.caption: Cathy Lynn Howley is a director of the Nova Scotia Health perioperative care network. (Nova Scotia Health/Submitted)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia

When the consultation and surgery wait times are combined, the total waits for hip and knee replacements in Nova Scotia are longer than they were a decade ago. In 2015, Nova Scotians could expect a total median wait of 265 days for a hip replacement — in 2025, it was 292 days.
Consultation times for hip and knee replacements soar, exceeding shortened surgery waits
N.S. surgical wait time data masks growing backlog of waiting patients
More than 500 days after Bruce Erskine was referred for a hip replacement surgery consultation, he still hadn’t spoken to a surgeon.

When his family doctor referred him in January 2025, he told Erskine the whole process should take about 18 months. Erskine, who lives in Halifax, has already passed that mark, without receiving a date for surgery.

Stuck in limbo, Erskine’s mobility and quality of life have quickly deteriorated. The previously active 75-year-old can no longer walk without a cane or take his young grandson to places they once enjoyed together.
“It's painful, physically and psychologically, because you're just sort of left to wait,” Erskine said.

A Canadian Institute for Health Information report released in June found wait times for hip and knee replacement surgeries were the shortest ever recorded in Nova Scotia, and some of the shortest reported in Canada last year.
But that report tracks only the period from surgical consultation to surgery date, and doesn’t measure the wait from referral to consulting a surgeon.
Nova Scotia slashes joint replacement wait times by 40%
Dr. Jhase Sniderman, an orthopedic surgeon at Dartmouth General Hospital, told CBC News in July that longer consultation waits leave patients with more pain and worse function.
“That has an impact on the rest of your health,” he said. “If you can't move around or walk, your muscles deteriorate. It's not good for your cardiovascular health either.”

Over the last decade, the median wait for a hip replacement consultation more than doubled, from 92 to 189 days. This increase erased progress made by shortening surgical wait times, which fell from 173 to 103 days over the same period.

Cathy Lynn Howley, a director of the Nova Scotia Health perioperative care network, said the reduced surgery wait times are a “real and significant improvement,” despite the total wait time growing worse.

“The progress that we're seeing in surgical access wait times is important, but it doesn't diminish the experience of someone who's still waiting months to see a surgeon,” she said. “And that's why we're broadening our focus to the entire patient journey.”
She said Nova Scotia Health needs to focus on improving consultation wait times, which are “too long” in some areas.

Nova Scotia’s rapidly growing and aging population likely contributed to longer consultation wait times, according to Howley. Despite surgeons in the province performing more hip replacements last year than any year on record, a surge in patients requiring orthopedic surgeries might be causing consultation backlogs.

items: Germany does more hip and knee replacements than Canada. What can we learn?
Electronic medical record rollout improves on 2nd pass, final launch looms in fall

blocks.text: Patients who spoke to CBC News reported worsening pain and deteriorating health while waiting for consultations.

Like Erskine, Monika Lalonde from Falmouth, N.S., has waited about 500 days for a hip replacement consultation. Unlike Erskine, who was assessed by a surgeon in June after a last-minute cancellation, Lalonde still doesn’t have a consultation appointment, never mind a surgery date.

“It's hard,” said Lalonde, who was previously told she would see a surgeon this summer. “In the meantime, pain has increased. My mobility's gone down to almost nothing. It's just gotten steadily worse.”
Golfing, gardening and dancing were once mainstays in Lalonde’s routine. Now, she says walking, bathing and getting dressed are difficult.
“I am 77 and realistically do not have many years left of my life, so it is a shame to spend them this way.”

blocks.caption: Cathy Lynn Howley is a director of the Nova Scotia Health perioperative care network. (Nova Scotia Health/Submitted)

blocks.text: The province’s new centralized booking system, which Howley partly credits for improving surgery waits, could help shorten consultation limbo. Over the last decade, the province has also opened orthopedic assessment clinics to help patients manage their pain while waiting for consultations.
Howley declined to disclose if Nova Scotia Health has an established plan to ease consultation waits.
“We’re still working through those plans,” she said. “There is work underway, certainly within Nova Scotia Health and within the perioperative program.”
That work can’t come fast enough for Lalonde, who has now waited almost 18 months for a hip replacement consultation, more than double the median wait time.
“I just feel like the health-care system has let me down,” she said. “I've been a very healthy person up to now, and now that I want to access the system, it's just not there for me.”
How does Nova Scotia measure up?
Most provinces don’t publicly report consultation wait times, but Nova Scotia is an outlier, displaying the estimated wait alongside the surgery wait on its website.

One in 10 patients who had a hip replacement consultation from January to March 2026 waited 517 days for the appointment. For the same period, one in 10 patients waited 279 days for the surgery itself.

That’s in stark contrast to Ontario, the province with the surgery wait time closest to Nova Scotia's. In Ontario, one in 10 patients seen in June 2026 waited 176 days for a hip replacement consultation and 218 days for surgery.

blocks.caption: Bruce Erskine waited more than 500 days to be assessed for hip replacement surgery by an orthopedic surgeon. (Eric Wiseman/CBC News)

blocks.text: Nova Scotians waited even longer for knee replacement consultations, with 50 per cent of patients seen from January to March 2026 waiting 261 days for a consult, and one in 10 waiting 615 days.
In Ontario, 50 per cent of patients seen in June 2026 waited 64 days for a consultation, with one in 10 patients waiting 190 days.

articles.title: PAGASA monitors 2 LPAs with potential to become tropical depressions
articles.summary: Two low-pressure areas (LPAs) are being monitored near the country, with both having a “medium chance” of developing into tropical depressions within the next 24 hours, the Philippine Atmospheric,…

blocks.text: Two low-pressure areas (LPAs) are being monitored near the country, with both having a “medium chance” of developing into tropical depressions within the next 24 hours, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Friday, Aug. 28.
The LPA designated as LPA 08i, which has been monitored since Thursday, Aug. 27, was located 560 kilometers east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes as of 2 p.m.
LPA 08i is expected to move toward Taiwan and is not forecast to make landfall over the Philippines.
Nevertheless, PAGASA said it continues to enhance the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” which is bringing rains over parts of Luzon.
Since LPA 08i is inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR), it will be given the local name “Pilandok” if it develops into a tropical depression.
Meanwhile, PAGASA said a new LPA designated as LPA 08j formed outside the PAR on Friday afternoon.
It was located 1,460 kilometers east of Central Luzon as of 2 p.m.
LPA 08j may also contribute to the strengthening of the habagat in the coming days.
If LPA 08j enters the PAR and develops into a tropical depression, it will be given the local name “Queenie.”
PAGASA said the enhanced southwest monsoon is expected to bring heavy rainfall over several Luzon areas this weekend.
From Friday to Saturday noon, Aug. 29, 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall, considered heavy to intense, may affect La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, and Occidental Mindoro.

Meanwhile, 50 to 100 millimeters of rainfall, considered moderate to heavy, may persist over Metro Manila, Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, Abra, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, and Oriental Mindoro.
From Saturday noon to Sunday noon, Aug. 30, 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall may continue over Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Benguet, Zambales, and Bataan.

Fifty to 100 millimeters of rainfall may prevail over Metro Manila, Ilocos Norte, Abra, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Oriental Mindoro.
From Sunday noon to Monday noon, Aug. 31, 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall may persist over Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, and Zambales.

Fifty to 100 millimeters of rainfall may affect Metro Manila, Batanes, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro.
PAGASA advised residents in areas that may experience heavy rainfall, particularly those prone to flooding and landslides, to remain alert and continue monitoring its latest weather updates.

articles.title: US judge rules Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic unlawful
articles.summary: The AI company was labeled a "supply chain risk" after refusing to allow unrestricted military use of its technology. The judge said "empty invocation of national security is not a blank check" to…

image.caption: Anthropic AI was labeled a 'supply chain risk' by the US government after refusing to allow unrestricted military use of its technologyImage: Jonathan Raa/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: A United States federal judge has ruled in favor of the artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic in its dispute with the Pentagon over its labeling as a "supply chain risk."

California district judge Rita Lin concluded that the label constituted an attempt by the government to make an example of Anthropic after the company refused to allow unrestricted military use of its technology and criticized the Department of Defense's use of AI.
Lin wrote in a 59-page ruling that "the empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics."

She said the government's actions were "based on a desire to make a public example out of Anthropic for its 'arrogance' in criticizing the government, not based on any articulable basis to believe that Anthropic would actually sabotage its model."

An Anthropic spokesperson said they welcomed the judge's ruling, saying in a statement: "We remain focused on working productively with the government to harness AI for our national security so all Americans benefit from this technology."
Anthropic AI: What is the Pentagon dispute all about?

The dispute between the San Francisco-based firm and the government broke out in February when President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth accused Anthropic of endangering national security after the company declined to allow unrestricted military use of its technology.

"We will not knowingly provide a product that puts America's warfighters and civilians at risk," wrote CEO Dario Amodei in a blog post back in February, adding that AI wasn't reliable enough to be used in fully autonomous weapons systems and expressing concerns over mass surveillance.
Anthropic AI shutdown — Security fears or power play?
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In March, the Pentagon designated Anthropic a "supply chain risk" – a highly unusual label to apply to a US firm. The company complained of an "unlawful campaign of retaliation," pointing out that the designation would have negative consequences for its business beyond defense deals.
Indeed, President Trump ordered all US government agencies to stop using Anthropic technology, calling it "a radical left, woke company" and "out-of-control" in a social media rant.
Defense Secretary Hegseth said companies would be expected to cut business links to Anthropic if they wanted to be considered for defense sector deals.
Shortly afterwards, OpenAI, Anthropic's primary tech industry rival and operator of ChatGPT, made its own deal to work with the Pentagon.
Anthropic ruling: What else did Judge Lin say?

In her ruling, Judge Lin, an appointee of former President Joe Biden, wrote that neither the US Constitution nor the federal statute the government invoked allows them to "impose sweeping penalties based principally on Anthropic's critique of the Administration's views."

Earlier in the legal proceedings, Lin had temporarily blocked the Pentagon from labeling the company as a supply chain risk and blocked enforcement of Trump's social media directive ordering all federal agencies to stop using Anthropic and its chatbot Claude.
In a preliminary hearing on July 30, Lin had said that the government's position was "really troubling" and seemed "at odds to me with the First Amendment."
The White House is yet to comment on the decision.

In the coming weeks, Anthropic is expected to launch on the US stock market with an initial public offering (IPO) that could potentially eclipse SpaceX's record Wall Street debut in June, which raised $86 billion (€74 billion).

articles.title: House damaged after dike gives way amid heavy rains in Zambales
articles.summary: SAN MARCELINO, Zambales — A house was damaged after a portion of a dike gave way, sending strong floodwaters into Barangay Sta. Fe amid continuous rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or habagat.…

blocks.text: house in Barangay Sta. Fe, San Marcelino, Zambales was damaged after a portion of the dike gave way, sending strong floodwaters into the area amid heavy rains brought by the habagat. The affected family was able to evacuate safely. (San Marcelino IO via Liezle Inigo)
SAN MARCELINO, Zambales — A house was damaged after a portion of a dike gave way, sending strong floodwaters into Barangay Sta. Fe amid continuous rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or habagat.
It was fortunate that the family residing in the house was able to evacuate safely before the situation worsened, according to the local government.
The barangay hall and other structures in the area are now under water, prompting authorities and response teams to closely monitor the situation.
San Marcelino Mayor Elvis Ragadio Soria urged residents to prioritize their safety and immediately evacuate to safer areas whenever necessary.
The local government also postponed the scheduled delivery of relief packs to Barangay Sta. Fe on Friday due to the unfavorable weather.
Authorities and response teams continue to monitor developments in Sta. Fe and assess the situation as heavy rains persist in the municipality.

articles.title: Dengue outbreak declared in Bohol
articles.summary: CEBU CITY–A dengue outbreak has been declared in Bohol Province, where at least 20 deaths linked to the mosquito-borne disease have been recorded for the past weeks. With this, Bohol Gov. Erico…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY–A dengue outbreak has been declared in Bohol Province, where at least 20 deaths linked to the mosquito-borne disease have been recorded for the past weeks.

With this, Bohol Gov. Erico Aristotle Aumentado issued an Executive Order (EO), directing all local government units (LGUs) in the province to ramp up efforts to prevent the disease from spreading further .
Aumentado also ordered to strengthen the monitoring and treatment of patients.
The Bohol Provincial Health Office (BPHO) reported that as of Aug. 22, 1,883 dengue cases have been reported. The figures are seven percent higher compared to the same period last year.
Provincial officials expressed concerns over the increasing fatalities.
Dr. Fruserma Mary Uy, head of the Bohol Provincial Health Office, said that while the number of cases is almost the same as last year, the number of deaths has increased significantly.
The total number of deaths is 1.17 percent higher compared to the same period last year, exceeding the Department of Health’s acceptable level of below one percent.
“Hopefully, it won’t increase any longer,” Uy said.

In Aumentado’s EO, LGUs were ordered to intensify the implementation of the 4S strategy against dengue, reactivate their local dengue task forces and conduct community-based activities aimed at eliminating mosquito breeding areas.
Hospitals and city and municipal health offices were also directed to establish Dengue Fast Lanes to help speed up consultation and treatment.

Niel John Oclarit, development management officer IV of the Provincial Department of Health Office-Bohol, said 12 of Bohol’s 48 LGUs have exceeded the dengue epidemic threshold for three consecutive weeks.
Talibon logged the highest number of cases with 188, followed by Tagbilaran City with 172 and Ubay with 146.
Getafe recorded 108 cases, while Tubigon had 99.
Talibon also recorded the highest fatalities five followed by Tubigon with three. Getafe and Ubay each recorded two deaths.

articles.title: DepEd strengthens monitoring of textbook distribution through LRMIS
articles.summary: After completing all its target textbook procurements for 2026, the Department of Education (DepEd) is enhancing the use of its Learning Resource Management and Information System (LRMIS) to closely…

blocks.text: (MB FILE PHOTO)

After completing all its target textbook procurements for 2026, the Department of Education (DepEd) is enhancing the use of its Learning Resource Management and Information System (LRMIS) to closely monitor the distribution of textbooks and teachers’ manuals in schools.

Recently, education department secured all 105 target textbook titles for public elementary and secondary schools. It covers the successive phases of curriculum implementation from Grades 1, 4, 7, and Senior High School in 2024; Grade 3 and Grades 2, 5, and 8 in 2025; and Grades 6, 9, and 10 in 2026.

The procurement, per DepEd, resolves long-standing bottlenecks flagged by the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II), which noted that DepEd procured only 27 of 88 required titles from 2014 to 2023.

DepEd said it will use the LRMIS to track the procurement and nationwide distribution of all 105 approved print and electronic textbook titles in real time, helping ensure that the learning materials reach schools and learners most in need.

According to DepEd Secretary Juan Edgardo Angara, the agency must now ensure that procured learning resources are tracked and accounted for throughout the distribution process and delivered to the schools, learners, and teachers that need them most.
“Natapos natin ang isang malaking bottleneck sa procurement. Pero hindi doon natatapos ang trabaho (We have resolved a major procurement bottleneck, but the work does not end there),” he said.

“Kailangan nating makita kung nasaan na ang textbooks, ilan ang hawak ng bawat school, anong grade level at learning area ang kulang, at saan puwedeng mag-reallocate kung may sobra o buffer stock. Iyan ang inaayos natin sa LRMIS (We need to determine where the textbooks are, how many each school has, which grade levels and learning areas lack materials, and where surplus or buffer stocks can be reallocated. That is what we are addressing through the LRMIS),” he added.
DepEd said achieving a one-to-one textbook-to-student ratio requires more than procuring enough textbooks.
It noted that enrollment changes every year across schools, grade levels, and localities, while textbooks may also be lost or damaged during their active use.

“Through LRMIS, schools may encode inventory data by learning resource, grade level, and learning area, which can be compared with current enrollment to identify gaps, verify deliveries, and guide the reallocation of available buffer stock,” the agency stated.

DepEd said the system offers a centralized database of learning resources, real-time inventory tracking, standardized reporting, and automated data-driven reports for schools, Schools Division Offices, Regional Offices, and the Central Office.

DepEd reported that as of Aug. 27, 37,705 public schools, or 78 percent of all schools under the department, had registered with the LRMIS, while 17,797 had recorded their textbook and teachers’ manual inventories in the system.
The latter figure accounted for about 37 percent of all DepEd schools and 77 percent of those covered by the current encoding phase, it added.
As such, the agency said schools encoded 20,520,035 learning resources in the system based on extracted regional inventory data.
Angara said encoding had been affected by bad weather in some areas, but the department remained committed to continuing the rollout without compromising school safety and operations.

“Habang mas maraming schools ang nag-e-encode, mas malinaw nating makikita kung saan kulang, saan sobra, at saan kailangang maglipat o magdagdag ng learning resources (As more schools encode their data, we will have a clearer picture of where learning resources are lacking, where there are surpluses, and where materials need to be transferred or increased),” he said.

articles.title: Teen boy allegedly messaged two others to join ‘degrading’ and ‘humiliating’ Sydney gang-rape, court hears
articles.summary:
Two 17-year-olds accused of subjecting teenage girl to hours-long sexual assault granted bail

  • Get our breaking…

blocks.text: Two boys allegedly invited to join a “degrading” and “humiliating” gang-rape in Sydney have been granted bail.
The pair are among three 17-year-olds accused of subjecting a teenage girl to an hours-long sexual assault on the night of 16 August.
The alleged instigator, a private school boy charged with 11 offences, allegedly took the girl to a football game and drinks before taking her to a home when she felt sick.
He is accused of raping her before a text message was sent to a friend, a children’s court was told on Friday.
He then invited another boy via text message to join in, with that boy attending to attack the girl, police prosecutor Sergeant Rhonda Riley alleged.
That boy has been charged with six counts of sexual assault in company as well as common assault.
The pair are alleged to have bragged about the attack to another friend, crudely telling him that he needed to have sex with the girl.
He responded to the invitation and arrived at the house and engaged in non-consensual sex with her, the court was told.
The third boy has been charged with two counts of aggravated sexual assault in company.
The alleged instigator did not apply for bail when his case was mentioned on Friday but his two co-accused did.
Children’s court judge Jeff Tunks was urged to consider that the teens had strong family supports, schooling commitments and lacked criminal histories.
Jai Rose, representing the second alleged attacker, said his client would abide by any bail conditions imposed.
Rose also pointed to the looming higher school certificate exams, prompting Sgt Riley to remark that the alleged victim would also have to complete her exams “going through fear, going through pain”.
The barrister for the third teen meanwhile suggested consent would be an issue at trial as a text after the alleged attack claimed the boy had not received necessary “context” from his co-accused.
Judge Tunks said social and sporting ties and exam delays were of little relevance to the bail assessment.
He described the alleged attack as “degrading” and a “humiliating” ordeal with “elements of menace”.
However, he granted bail to the two co-accused, finding the risks posed by the pair could be mitigated with strict conditions.
“The bail act is not used as some sort of de facto punishment for crimes that are not proven beyond reasonable doubt,” Judge Tunks said.
Both teens were ordered to be of good behaviour, report to police daily and abide by a home detention condition.
They were instructed not to contact each other or witnesses, surrender travel documents and possess only one phone.
The alleged instigator remains in juvenile detention.
He faces the most charges, including six counts of aggravated sexual assault in company and three counts of sexual intercourse without consent.
The teens’ cases return to court in October.

articles.title: Baguio police, cybercrime unit initiate takedown of bullying posts
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY – The Baguio City Police Office (BCPO) and the Cybercrime Unit are now taking appropriate action to begin the process of removing posts and videos online related to alleged incidents of…

blocks.text: (Baguio PIO via Zaldy Comanda)

BAGUIO CITY – The Baguio City Police Office (BCPO) and the Cybercrime Unit are now taking appropriate action to begin the process of removing posts and videos online related to alleged incidents of violence involving students from two public high schools in the city.

BCPO City Director P Col Ruel Tagel said the move covers posts and videos circulating online that are related to the two separate incidents involving minors including an account that had posted details of some of the minors involved and appeared to be inciting violence including grave threats.

The city government and the Pinget National High School, even the Department of Education (DepEd)-Baguio had earlier appealed to the public to take down and refrain from posting and sharing the videos, as the incidents involved minors wary that continued circulation could expose the children to public shaming, harassment, insults, threats and other forms of online abuse.

Mayor Benjamin Magalong said the two cases are being handled separately, with police coordinating with concerned school authorities and social workers. The students involved have also been identified.

He encouraged the public to allow the police, school authorities and social workers to address the incidents through proper intervention while respecting the privacy, dignity and well-being of the minors involved.

blocks.text: The Nepali army has been working to rescue survivors who had been trapped inside a tunnel at a hydropower project in Rasuwa.
Footage shared by the country's prime minister office shows soliders carrying survivors and crawling across thick slates of mud to reach others.
An update issued by officials on Thursday indicated more than 100 people were estimated to have been trapped in the same tunnel.
It forms part of rescue efforts being carried out across the country in the wake of the flood as hundreds of people have died and many are still missing.

articles.title: Bike patrol at Bacolod-Silay airport launched to boost security, cut fuel use
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY - Police at the Bacolod-Silay Airport have intensified their patrol operations in and around the airport premises, following the launch of a bicycle patrol initiative aimed at…

blocks.text: The Bacolod-Silay Airport Police in Silay City, Negros Occidental, has recently launched a bike patrol initiative to strengthen police visibility in and around the airport while promoting health, fitness, and environmental sustainability. (Bacolod-Silay Airport)

BACOLOD CITY - Police at the Bacolod-Silay Airport have intensified their patrol operations in and around the airport premises, following the launch of a bicycle patrol initiative aimed at strengthening security and police visibility.

Dubbed the “Padyak ng Pulisya sa Paliparan Project” (4P’s), the initiative seeks to promote physical fitness and camaraderie among police personnel while enhancing security through mobile, foot, and bicycle patrols.

Police Major Deejay Domingo, chief of the Bacolod-Silay Airport police, said the bike patrol allows personnel to reinforce security in the area while promoting physical wellness and an eco-friendly approach to police operations.
The initiative is also expected to help reduce the unit’s fuel consumption amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East.
The program is being implemented under the supervision of Police Col. Alex Dimaculangan, chief of the Aviation Security Unit-Negros Island Region (NIR).

As part of the launching activities, police personnel also distributed rice to airport security guards through the station’s community outreach program, highlighting the unit’s commitment to public service and stronger partnerships with airport stakeholders.

The Bacolod-Silay Airport currently has 11 bicycles for the patrol initiative. Similar bike patrol operations are also being implemented in Negros Oriental, with two bicycles assigned in Dumaguete City and two in Siquijor.
Domingo said bike patrols at the airport will be conducted randomly to avoid establishing a predictable pattern and further strengthen security operations.

articles.title: PNP readies units for AI-enabled body cameras
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) said Friday, Aug. 28, that it was gearing up for the deployment of new body-worn cameras powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that were expected to provide…

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) said Friday, Aug. 28, that it was gearing up for the deployment of new body-worn cameras powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that were expected to provide clearer records of police encounters and operations in the field.

Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., PNP chief, said the equipment would give police officers a more reliable record of their interactions with the public while helping preserve evidence and support investigations.

“The AI-enabled body cameras will enhance the PNP’s capability to document police operations with clearer and more reliable footage. This will help preserve evidence, support investigations, and promote greater accountability among our personnel,” Nartatez said.

Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla earlier told the House committee on appropriations during a briefing on the proposed DILG budget for 2027 that the PNP is procuring 10,000 to 20,000 new AI-enabled body-worn cameras this year.
The new cameras are expected to have better lenses and improved image quality to make the footage more suitable for AI processing.
The procurement has already been bid out, he said, and more cameras will also be purchased annually as the PNP expands the use of the technology among its personnel.
For his part, Nartatez said the cameras would also serve as protection for police officers by providing an objective record of what happens during encounters and operations.
“This technology will protect not only the public but also our police officers by providing an objective record of what transpired during police encounters and operations,” the PNP chief said.
He said the police organization would make sure that the equipment is used properly and within existing rules.

“We assure the public that these body cameras will be used to strengthen transparency and accountability in police operations. We will ensure that our personnel use the technology properly and in accordance with existing laws and policies,” Nartatez added.

articles.title: Norway’s King Harald dies aged 89
articles.summary:
Monarch’s death comes at turbulent time for royal family over association of crown princess with Jeffrey Epstein

King Harald V of Norway, Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, has died aged 89,…

blocks.text: King Harald V of Norway, Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, has died aged 89, the royal palace in Oslo has announced. He was succeeded immediately by his son, King Haakon VIII.

“It is with deep sadness that we announce that His Majesty King Harald passed away today. King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University hospital on Friday 28 August at 6.35am,” the palace said in a statement.

The new king, whose wife, Mette-Marit, has recently come under scrutiny over scandals including a much-criticised association with the late US child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, formally notified the government of his father’s death on Friday.

As crowds gathered outside the royal palace to pay their respects, the government announced a period of national mourning. Flags around the country were lowered to half mast and church bells rang out at midday.

Haakon, 53, formally told government ministers of his father’s death at an extraordinary council of state on Friday morning. As expected, he said he would take the name Haakon VIII, and he chose the personal motto: “Everything for Norway”.

The new king will swear an oath of accession in parliament within the next few days. Coronation ceremonies were abolished in Norway more than a century ago, but Haakon could choose to have his reign blessed at a consecration ceremony.

The palace had said on Thursday that Harald’s health had deteriorated and that the king, who was seen as a unifying figure and a force for stability amid a string of recent family scandals, was in an “extremely serious” condition.

blocks.caption: King Harald during a welcoming ceremony for the Danish king and queen in Oslo in May 2024. Photograph: Per Ole Hagen/Getty Images

blocks.text: Norway’s prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, said he had received the news “with deep sadness”. “A whole nation is in mourning, and ⁠the people of Norway are left with a ​deep sense of ‌gratitude for a ‌long life in the service of Norway,” he said.
Støre added: “Harald V demonstrated an unwavering faith in the Norwegian people. He helped us to see the best in ourselves, and in one another … King Harald loved Norway. And Norway loved its king.”

Royalty around Europe sent their condolences, with Spain’s royal family hailing Harald’s “responsibility, dignity, humility and tireless dedication”, and Denmark’s King Frederik and Queen Mary saying he was “loved like few others”.

King Carl XVI Gustaf, of Sweden, said: “Throughout the years, King Harald has been a good friend to me, my family, and to Sweden … I ​wish ​my dear godson Haakon, ​who now succeeds his father as head ​of state, ‌success and ​good ​fortune.”

Belgium’s royal family recalled Harald’s “humour, humanity and sincerity”, while Britain’s King Charles mourned the loss of his “dear cousin”, paying tribute to a “towering figure” who guided his country with “warmth and humility”.

blocks.caption: People gather at Palace Square in Oslo to pay their respects to King Harald. Photograph: Rune Hellestad/Getty

blocks.text: The European Commission chief, Ursula von der Leyen, said he “brought Norwegians together”. Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said Norway had “lost a great figure who stood for prudence and unity”, and the French president, Emmanuel Macron, expressed “deep sadness”.
Norway’s ceremonial head of state since 1991, Harald was being treated for haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of the body’s red blood cells.

He had had numerous health problems – an operation for bladder cancer in 2003 and a pacemaker fitted in 2024 – but always ruled out abdicating, saying he had taken a lifelong oath before the Norwegian parliament.

His death comes amid a turbulent period for Norway’s royal family. Documents published in the US in January showed that Mette-Marit corresponded with Epstein between 2011 and 2014, long after he was convicted.

blocks.caption: Haakon had taken on additional royal duties while his father was ill. Photograph: Per Ole Hagen/Getty

blocks.text: The files appeared to contain almost 1,000 mentions of Mette-Marit, including intimate exchanges. They drew fierce public criticism, with Støre accusing her in unprecedented comments of “poor judgment”.
after newsletter promotion

Mette-Marit subsequently released a statement via the royal household expressing her “deepest regret for my friendship with Jeffrey Epstein” and apologising for “the situation that I have put the royal family in, especially the king and queen”.

blocks.caption: Mette-Marit had a successful lung transplant in July. Photograph: Lise Åserud/NTB Scanpix/AP

blocks.text: Marius Borg Høiby, 29, Mette-Marit’s son from a previous relationship, has also been in the spotlight after being sentenced in June to four years in prison for two rapes and 32 other charges, including violence against a former partner. He has appealed.

The scandals have affected public support for Norway’s monarchy, with a poll in February finding support down to 54% from 72% in 2024. Several polls found nearly half of the population felt Mette-Marit could not become queen.

Harald was seen as the Norwegian monarchy’s great moderniser, revamping the crown estates and changing the way the court is run. He married Sonja, a commoner, in 1968 and welcomed two others, Mette-Marit and Ari Behn, as the spouses of his children.

A great-great-grandchild ‌of Britain’s Queen Victoria, he succeeded his father, Olav V, at the age of 54 after studying at Oxford and representing his country in sailing events at the Tokyo, Mexico City and Munich Olympics. He was widely appreciated in Norway for his unassuming lifestyle and commitment to national unity.

blocks.caption: Haakon and Mette-Marit watching the 2026 World Cup match between Norway and Brazil. Photograph: The royal court/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: In an emotional speech in 2011 after the far-right extremist Anders Behring Breivik killed 77 in two terror attacks, he told his subjects that “freedom is stronger than fear” and as “a father, grandfather and spouse, I can only begin to sense some of the pain you feel. As king of the nation, I feel for every one of you.”

In a widely praised 2016 speech, he lauded diversity, tolerance and LGBTQ+ rights, saying Norwegians came from Afghanistan and Pakistan, believed “in God, in Allah and in nothing”, and included “girls who love girls, boys who love boys and girls and boys who love each other”.

blocks.caption: King Harald and Queen Sonja at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, Italy. Photograph: Heiko Junge/Reuters

blocks.text: Mette-Marit, 53, who has a serious lung disease and had a transplant in July, was a single mother to Høiby, who was four years old when her engagement to Norway’s crown prince was announced in late 2000.

The marriage, which marked the first time in modern European history that a direct heir to a throne had brought a stepson into a royal family, caused huge controversy in Norway but was strongly backed by King Harald and Queen Sonja.

Mette-Marit acknowledged having what she described as a rebellious youth and prior drug use, holding an emotional press conference a week before the wedding in which she expressed regret for her choices and strongly condemned drug use.

articles.title: Norway's King Harald dies at 89
articles.summary: King Harald is succeeded by his son, who has taken the name King Haakon VIII, with Crown Princess Mette-Marit now queen.

image.caption: Prince Harald was born on 21 February 1937Image: Fredrik Varfjell/NTB/AFP

blocks.text: Norway's King Harald, Europe's oldest living monarch, has died at 89, the royal court said on Friday.
The monarch had been receiving treatment for a rare blood condition, hemolytic anemia, at Oslo University Hospital since mid-August.
His son, Prince Haakon automatically becomes King Haakon VIII, with the Norwegian Royal Court also confirming on Thursday that his wife, Mette-Marit, will become queen.
The Norwegian monarch is head of state, but has a largely ceremonial and representative role.
What the palace said about King Harald's death

"It is with deep sadness that we announce that His Majesty King Harald passed away today. King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University Hospital on Friday, August 28 at 6:35 a.m.," the palace said in a statement.
Harald's condition worsened over the last few days, and his wife, Queen Sonja, and son, Haakon, canceled all their engagements to be at his bedside.

Harald, who had been king since 1991, suffered a series of health problems in recent years and had increasingly scaled back his official duties. However, he repeatedly ruled out abdicating, saying the oath he had taken on becoming king "lasts for life."

blocks.caption: People gathered for a night vigil at the Palace Square in OsloImage: Odd Andersen/AFP

blocks.text: Hundreds of well-wishers gathered outside the royal palace in Oslo overnight, holding a vigil as the king's condition deteriorated.
World leaders, royals pay tribute
Britain's King Charles expressed his condolences for Harald's death, paying tribute to a "towering figure" who guided his country with "warmth and humility."
Norway's prime minister, Jonas Gahr Stoere, said Harald demonstrated an "unwavering faith in the Norwegian people" and "helped us to see the best in ourselves – and in one another."
Swedish King Carl XVI Gustaf said the late king had "been a good friend" and would be "mourned by many in our country."
"I wish my dear Godson Haakon, who now succeeds his father as head of state, success and good fortune in the important role that lies ahead of ‌him," he added.

King Frederik and Queen Mary of Denmark praised Harald's "warm personality and rock-solid calm," saying he "combined duty and responsibility with presence and humanity. He was loved like few others and will be missed by many."
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described him as "a true European and a lifelong servant of his people."
"In moments of joy and sorrow, he brought Norwegians together," she said.
NATO chief Mark Rutte said Harald "showed himself to be a dedicated leader. His own military roots made him a champion of the Norwegian military and a long-time friend of NATO."
How will King Harald be remembered?

Born in 1937, Harald became Norway's first prince to be born in the country in more than 500 years. As a child, he fled Norway with his mother and sisters following the Nazi invasion in 1940, spending much of World War II in the United States.

Harald succeeded his father, King Olav V, in January 1991 and went on to modernize the Norwegian monarchy during more than 35 years on the throne. He was widely praised for his response to the 2011 far-right terrorist attacks that killed 77 people and later drew attention for speeches stressing tolerance, diversity and LGBTQ+ equality.
The king's death comes after a turbulent period for Norway's royal family.

blocks.caption: King Harald V waves during a 1991 coronation tour after his accession to the throneImage: Lise Åserud/NTB/picture alliance

blocks.text: Crown Princess [nonw Queen] Mette-Marit has faced scrutiny over her past correspondence with the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Her son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Hoiby, was sentenced in June to four years in prison after being convicted of two rapes and dozens of other offenses, including violence against a former partner. He has appealed the verdict.
Edited by: Natalie Muller

articles.title: Suguilon assumes post as new PRO 13 chief
articles.summary: CAMP RAFAEL C. RODRIGUEZ, Butuan City – Brig. Gen. Rolindo M. Suguilon has been designated regional director of the Police Regional Office 13 (PRO 13) based here effective Friday, Aug. 28. Suguilon…

blocks.text: CAMP RAFAEL C. RODRIGUEZ, Butuan City – Brig. Gen. Rolindo M. Suguilon has been designated regional director of the Police Regional Office 13 (PRO 13) based here effective Friday, Aug. 28.
Suguilon officially assumed command of PRO 13 during a turnover of office ceremony held at the police regional headquarters PRO 13 Multi-Purpose Center here.

Police Lt. Gen. Bernard M. Banac, Deputy Chief PNP for Administration (TDCA), served as the Presiding Officer on behalf of the Chief of the Philippine National Police, Police General Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr.

A member of the Philippine National Police Academy (PNPA) “Patnubay” Class of 1995, Brig. Gen. Suguilon previously served as director of the PNP Training Service (PNPTS) prior to his assignment in Northeastern Mindanao or The Caraga Region.

In his assumption message, the new top poliee official in Northestern Mindanao assured the public that he will protect, preserve, and sustain the hard-earned peace established by his predecessors at the helm of the Caraga region police force.

“To the people of Caraga, I embrace this command as a solemn commitment to God, country, and the Filipino people,” Brig. Gen. Suguilon said, adding “Together—as one disciplined, dedicated, and community-centered police force—let us build a safer, more peaceful, and more prosperous Caraga for all”.
Meanwhile, the outgoing Caraga Regional Director, Police Brig. Gen. Marcial Mariano P. Magistrado IV, will be reassigned to the Directorate for Comptrollership.

articles.title: Japan’s JCR keeps Philippines’ A- rating, sees return to high growth
articles.summary: Tokyo-based Japan Credit Rating Agency Ltd. (JCR) maintained the Philippines’ credit rating at “A-” with a stable outlook as the debt watcher projects that the domestic economy will return to “high…

blocks.text: Tokyo-based Japan Credit Rating Agency Ltd. (JCR) maintained the Philippines’ credit rating at “A-” with a stable outlook as the debt watcher projects that the domestic economy will return to “high growth” rates, with initial signs of recovery surfacing in the second half of 2026.

Despite Philippine economic expansion slumping to a post-pandemic low of 2.6 percent in the first half due to high consumer prices and public construction delays, JCR still expects growth to rebound in the second half on the back of resumed spending and tamer inflation.
According to JCR, a stronger macroeconomic performance is on the horizon, with the agency projecting inflation-adjusted gross domestic product (GDP) growth to recover from July to December.
Local growth is expected to average around 3.5 percent, buoyed by the “recovery in public infrastructure investment and the effects of price stabilization policies.”

This projected turnaround follows a challenging first half of the year, during which unpredictable geopolitical headwinds and state spending bottlenecks stalled output expansion. Economic growth averaged 2.6 percent in the first half, marking a post-pandemic low.

Data showed the slowdown was driven by sluggish public investments and muted household consumption. Exacerbating this was inflation, which averaged 4.8 percent in the same period due to spikes in oil and food prices amid the ongoing war between the United States (US) and Iran.

Even with these pressures, JCR remains optimistic about the Philippines’ structural resilience and ongoing economic reforms. Beyond 2026, JCR is betting on improvements in the investment climate, propped up by the state’s efforts.

“JCR believes that, as the government works to improve the investment environment and advance industrial upgrading, the economy will return to high growth rates over the medium term,” it said in a rating action statement published Friday, Aug. 28.
This positive medium-term outlook is banking on the government’s commitment to restoring fiscal discipline.

To anchor investor confidence, the Marcos Jr. administration aims to lower the fiscal deficit-to-GDP ratio to 3.5 percent and the central government debt-to-GDP ratio to 63.1 percent by 2030 by streamlining government spending and pursuing major tax overhauls.
Achieving these milestones will require navigating a slower fiscal consolidation path in the near term due to recent delays in public works and elevated commodity prices.

As of end-2025, the national government’s (NG) debt ratio stood at 62.2 percent. While historically this was close to record highs, JCR noted that this level is relatively low compared with sovereigns rated in the “A” range.
JCR said the government debt-to-GDP ratio is expected to remain in the mid-60-percent range for some time before gradually declining toward the administration’s long-term targets.

Finance Secretary Frederick D. Go said the Japanese debt watcher’s nod to the country’s investment-grade rating and stable outlook “reflects the resilience of our economy and the government’s commitment to fiscal consolidation and long-term reforms.”
“It reinforces investor confidence and supports our efforts to attract investments, create quality jobs, and sustain inclusive growth,” Go further said.

Further, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) also welcomed the credit rating affirmation, saying this “reflects continued confidence in the country’s sound fundamentals amid external headwinds,” particularly the heightened uncertainty, including the Middle East conflict.

“For its part, the BSP will continue to promote price stability, safeguard financial stability, and ensure safe and efficient payments and settlements,” the central bank said. “These efforts support sustainable growth and broader economic opportunities for Filipinos.”

articles.title: Legarda thanks Antique legislature for support
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY— Senator Loren Legarda has thanked the Antique Provincial Board for showing formal support while she is on extended medical leave abroad. This was after the Antique Provincial Board…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY— Senator Loren Legarda has thanked the Antique Provincial Board for showing formal support while she is on extended medical leave abroad.

This was after the Antique Provincial Board passed Resolution 775-2026 that expressed the collective “sincere gratitude, appreciation, and support to Senator Legarda for her exemplary public service and significant contributions to the Filipino people, particularly to the people of Antique”.

“Malaki ang kahulugan nito sa akin, lalo na sa panahong ito, at makakaasa ang aking mga kasimanwa na mananatili akong matatag sa paglilingkod at nakatuon sa kapakanan ng Antique at ng ating bansa (This means a great deal to me, especially at this time, and my fellow Antiqueños can rest assured that I will remain steadfast in service and focused on the welfare of Antique and our country),” said Legarda in a statement.
It was in 2019 to 2022 when Legarda served as congresswoman of the Lone District of Antique, the home province of her maternal grandfather.
Legarda was replaced by her younger brother AA as congressional representative of Antique in 2022 when she won a Senate seat during the 2022 elections.
For nearly a decade, Legarda was able to bring in big ticket projects to Antique.
The resolution noted Legarda’s “meaningful connection with the Province of Antique and has supported various programs, initiatives, and advocacies that have contributed to the welfare, development.”

The resolution was introduced by Vice Governor Genevive Lim-Reyes and sponsored by Provincial Board Memebrs Gaseva V. Recopuerto, Joseph Eugene D. Alojipan, Emmanuel C. Palacios, Jr., Alfie Jay O. Niquia, Kenneth Dave B. Gasalao, and Julius Cezar O. Tajanlangit.

The collective sentiment of the provincial legislature also lauded Legarda for having “consistently championed advocacies on environmental protection, climate change adaptation and disaster resilience, cultural heritage, education, sustainable development, and the preservation of the country's natural and cultural resources.”

articles.title: Peso plunges past ₱62:$1 to new record low of ₱62.265
articles.summary: Demand for the safe-haven United States (US) dollar surged amid heightened geopolitical uncertainty, sending the Philippine peso tumbling to a fresh historic low of ₱62.265 on Friday, Aug. 28, from…

blocks.text: Demand for the safe-haven United States (US) dollar surged amid heightened geopolitical uncertainty, sending the Philippine peso tumbling to a fresh historic low of ₱62.265 on Friday, Aug. 28, from the previous record of ₱61.888 just a day ago.

The local currency slid to an intraday low of ₱62.27 and hit a high of ₱62 after opening at ₱62.05. Total trading volume climbed to $1.962 billion from Thursday’s $1.79 billion, according to the Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP).

Singapore-based DBS Bank Ltd. noted that the Philippine peso was the only Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)-6 currency to weaken against the greenback so far in the third quarter of 2026, declining by 0.8 percent, while its regional peers appreciated by 0.9 to 1.7 percent over the same period.

Reyes Tacandong & Co. senior adviser Jonathan Ravelas said the US dollar-peso pair rose again “after the greenback strengthened anew on Middle East worries and ahead of the Jackson Hole speech by US Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh.”

Similarly, Ruben Carlo O. Asuncion, chief economist at Union Bank of the Philippines (UnionBank), cited the dominance of offshore developments rather than domestic developments. “Markets remain focused on broad US dollar strength, elevated oil prices, and lingering uncertainty in global financial markets,” he said.

Asuncion noted that the local currency still slipped even as the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) decided to further raise key borrowing costs by a quarter point to five percent—a move that typically supports the currency.

“Demand for dollars from importers and investors has also likely contributed to the peso’s weakness,” Asuncion said, noting that the net oil-importing country remains vulnerable during periods of a sustained rally in the greenback.

“More broadly, the peso’s recent weakness is consistent with the challenges often faced by emerging market (EM) and regional currencies during periods of dollar strength and heightened global uncertainty,” he added.

Ravelas expects the currency pair to trade within the range of ₱61.9 to ₱62.3 despite the support from the BSP’s tightening. He said geopolitical risks are expected to continue driving this dimmer outlook for the peso.

articles.title: Role of infrastrusture, farmers' empowerment underscored in agri sector development
articles.summary: DAVAO CITY – Cotabato Governor Emmylou Taliño-Mendoza has underscored the vital role of reliable infrastructure as well as empowerment of farmers in the development of the agriculture sector. In her…

blocks.text: DAVAO CITY – Cotabato Governor Emmylou Taliño-Mendoza has underscored the vital role of reliable infrastructure as well as empowerment of farmers in the development of the agriculture sector.

In her speech before the delegates of the 14th National Palm Oil Congress here, Mendoza also emphasized the role of local governments, saying that it should never be just limited to distributing planting materials and farm inputs.

The local government, she said, must become an ecosystem builder while the Department of Agriculture (DA) provides national policy and resources; banks provide financing; and private companies provide technology as well as market access.
Mendoza said that local governments should turn farmers into productive assets to avoid creating dependency.

“The government provides the right starting input, the knowledge, and the technical support. But the farmer takes responsibility for the investment,” she said while referring to the provincial government’s program called Plant Now, Take Care (PNTC).
Under the program, the provincial government distributes high-quality oil palm seedlings to qualified local farmers.

She explained that under the scheme, beneficiaries who could successfully achieve an 85% survival rate for the seedlings during the first year, they do not have to pay back or return the cost of the planting materials.

From 2012 to 2026, according to the governor, the PNTC investments have reached approximately P272 million, benefiting 3,640 farmers and establishing 7,497.94 hectares of oil palm across the province.
In 2026 alone, Mendoza added, the program allocated P35 million, benefiting 521 farmers and establishing approximately 942.5 hectares of oil palm farms.
“These are not just numbers in a government accomplishment report. They represent farms. They represent families,” she said before the delegates.
When government assistance is linked to responsibility, accountability, and actual farm productivity, the governor further said, public resources transform into long-term economic assets.
Mendoza also called for stronger cooperatives and farmer organizations to be able to aggregate production, negotiate better terms, access financing as well as a better transport system.
Moreover, Mendoza also underscored the role of reliable infrastructures in the development of the oil palm industry since its produce is particularly dependent on efficient logistics.

“That means farm-to-market roads matter. Bridges, collection points, hauling facilities, drainage and transport matters,” she said before the delegates of the two-day event that culminated today, August 28.

Mendoza also noted that agricultural policy and infrastructure policy cannot be treated separately. “Infrastructure must follow the value chain. And the provincial government will continue to advocate for infrastructure investments.”

Under the Department of Agriculture's Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP) Scale-Up, Mendoza said, the province has a portfolio of approximately P996 million in priority infrastructure and water-system investments aimed at improving connectivity, water access, and rural productivity.

“These are not merely construction projects. If properly planned, they become economic infrastructure. They reduce logistics costs. They improve market access. They make farms more viable. And they make investment more attractive,” she added.
Furthermore, the governor also acknowledged the role of technology in producing reliable data in the agriculture sector.
Mendoza said that farmers should maximize all available modern technology such as drones, remote sensing, farm monitoring systems and data-driven fertilizer application,
She also emphasized the value of having accurate data to be able to appropriately respond to the needs of farmers.

Organized by the Philippine Palm Oil Development Council, Inc, the event gathered industry leaders, experts, stakeholders, and partners for a two-day discussion on networking opportunities, and the latest developments in the Philippine palm oil industry.

articles.title: Palace: Philippines won’t enter deals that put Filipinos at a disadvantage
articles.summary: Malacañang assured the public that President Marcos will not enter into any deal with another country that would put the Philippines and its people at a disadvantage. "Nagsalita din po ang Pangulo,…

blocks.text: Malacañang assured the public that President Marcos will not enter into any deal with another country that would put the Philippines and its people at a disadvantage.

"Nagsalita din po ang Pangulo, hindi maaaring gumawa ng anumang transaksyon na ang Pilipinas o mga Pilipino ang siyang madidehado (The President also said that no transaction should be made if it would put the Philippines or Filipinos at a disadvantage)," Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro said in a recent Palace briefing.
She made the statement after the United States imposed hefty tariffs on Canada for refusing to agree to a trade deal that would grant the former exclusive access to its critical minerals.

Given that the US-led Pax Silica is making its way to the Philippines, the Palace official was asked what safeguards Manila has put in place to ensure that Washington will equally respect the Philippines' demands.
Castro did not cite a specific measure, but assured the public that the Marcos administration will only carry out projects and deals according to laws.
She also stressed that just because the government is pursuing investments does not mean that it will allow Filipinos to suffer.

"Kailangan po natin na magkaroon ng mga investments pero hindi nangangahulugan na ang ating mga kapuwa Pilipino ang magdurusa (We need to attract investments, but that does not mean our fellow Filipinos should suffer as a result)," Castro said.

"So maliwanag po iyan, hindi po natin pababayaan kung ano ang itinatalaga ng ating batas, hindi po natin iba-violate ang karapatan ng ating mga kapwa nating Pilipino (So, that is clear: we will not disregard what is mandated by our laws, and we will not violate the rights of our fellow Filipinos)," Castro added.

articles.title: PNP weighs home inspections for gov’t firearms, backs campus security law amid school shootings
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police said Friday, Aug. 28, it will conduct further study and consultations with stakeholders on the proposal to inspect residences where government-issued firearms are kept…

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police said Friday, Aug. 28, it will conduct further study and consultations with stakeholders on the proposal to inspect residences where government-issued firearms are kept as authorities seek to prevent weapons from being accessed by minors and used in school attacks.

Police General Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr. said the measure aims to compel firearm holders to be more responsible and compliant with conditions of gun ownership but he stressed that consultations must be held to ensure privacy rights are not compromised.

“We are in the process of strengthening our measures to ensure that government-issued weapons are properly stored and kept. This will be carefully studied and we assure that the concerns and sentiments of all the sectors involved will be respected and factored in,” Nartatez said, noting that the police organization will coordinate with the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) for the guidelines of the proposal.

DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla earlier proposed during the House committee hearing on the budget of the agency that police should be allowed to conduct an inspection in the homes of individuals who had government-issued firearms to ensure they are properly stored and kept away from unauthorized persons.
He later clarified that inspections would not be conducted through search warrants but through waivers signed by gun owners, with one day’s notice.

The push for tighter firearm controls followed two school shooting incidents in Tacloban City on June 22 and Zamboanga City on Aug. 18 involving minor students who gained access to firearms that turned out to be government-issued.
Nartatez said any inspection scheme should have clear procedures and safeguards as these should protect the rights of gun owners and police officers from any form of harassment.
He also assured the public that the PNP would keep any action within existing laws and respect individual rights.
PNP backs Comprehensive School Safety Act
Meanwhile, the PNP also expressed support for a proposed law that seeks to strengthen security measures in schools following recent school shootings.

Nartatez said Senate Bill No. 2426, or the Comprehensive School Safety Act, filed by Sen. Bam Aquino, seeks to establish a nationwide system for school safety and provide sustained funding for campus protection programs.

“We support measures that strengthen the protection of our learners. The PNP is ready to work closely with DepEd [Department of Education] and other stakeholders to ensure that schools remain safe and secure environments,” Nartatez said.

The measure covers prevention, response and recovery programs including risk assessments, safety training, emergency procedures, and active safety drills. It also provides for psychosocial and mental health support for affected students, families, and school personnel.

“School safety must be preventive, responsive, and supportive. We will continue strengthening police visibility, threat assessment, emergency preparedness, and coordination with school authorities,” Nartatez said.
The proposed legislation would also complement existing DepEd and PNP efforts such as the School Safety Campaign, stricter campus inspections, visitor management, and increased police patrols.

“Our first priority will be to ensure seamless coordination with DepEd and local stakeholders and to strengthen our police units’ capability to prevent and respond to threats against schools,” he said.

articles.title: The only time The Dog Stars isn't boring is when it's bad
articles.summary: The Dog Stars is about the same thing as every other post-apocalypse film you've seen, but this time without the guts or energy to make it believably harrowing.

image.caption: Jacob Elordi plays Hig in The Dog Stars, a film adapted from a book written by Peter Heller. (20th Century Studios/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·REVIEW
The Dog Stars is about the same thing as every other post-apocalypse film you've seen, but this time without the guts or energy to make it believably harrowing.
Adaptation of Peter Heller's post-apocalyptic novel misses the mark

blocks.caption: Jacob Elordi plays Hig in The Dog Stars, a film adapted from a book written by Peter Heller. (20th Century Studios/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: The Dog Stars is about many things and most of them are not very fun to think about.

It is about failed ambition; that of an out-of-practice, middle-aged, unread poet forced into a career of manual labour he neither enjoys or appreciates. It is about the pointlessness of ambition; of that same man later eking out a life in the post-apocalypse — haunted more by his unkillable hope for something better than by the jerky made of human corpses he feeds his dog.

And it is about that survivor and his dog flying in their beat-up Cessna over the ruined remains of the world while vainly trying to find beauty in it. And being nearly broken when they fail. But then sometimes finding something beautiful after all — and that, somehow, hurting even more.
At least, that is what The Dog Stars by Peter Heller is about; a lyrically dour novel about a post-epidemic wasteland told through the eyes of our writer-turned-pilot, dog-loving hero, Hig.

But when it comes to the Ridley Scott-directed adaptation, it is more about a Jacob Elordi-shaped cardboard cutout version of Hig, stoically bearing the world on his shoulders with a sideways smile. Carrying the flame of humanity all on his own, in whichever hand isn't already tightened around a hammer, wrench or plane yoke to yet again save someone else's day.

It's about a 20-something-year-old, virile Everyman upon whose shoulder we sit, to be ferried from gun battle to maudlin monologue and back again. About the after-school-special style of hope in the face of horror. About distracting, inappropriate to the plot (but necessary to studio heads) action in place of drama.

It's about laughably contrived scavengers mowed down by our protagonists like target practice — genre-appropriate targets made up to look either like the Lost Boys from Hook, or whatever banged-up "War Boys" they could still find kicking around the set of Mad Max: Fury Road.
In essence, it's about the same thing as every other, more successful post-apocalypse films you've seen, but this time without the guts or energy to make it believably harrowing.
Which is all somewhat funny. Because when not comparing it against the critically acclaimed, imposingly successful novel, The Dog Stars is… still a disappointment.

Starting out following Elordi's Hig as an I Am Legend-type city-scavenger, it at least has the aesthetics of a survival drama. And as we meet mule-stubborn Bangley (Josh Brolin), Hig's irascible soldier-of-fortune compound companion, we get the beginnings of a fairly competent buddy film. One rooted in the chemistry between bristled, but (obviously) secretly vulnerable Bangley — a balance capably pulled off by an actor that, from Deadpool to No Country For Old Men, long-ago cornered the market on this archetype.

blocks.caption: Josh Brolin plays Bangley, Hig's irascible soldier-of-fortune compound companion in The Dog Stars (20th Century Studios/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: But it's one impressive performance undercut by Elordi: an actor who, like Sydney Sweeney in The Housemaid, feels so self-consciously resistant to the idea of interiority that every performance could be described with either the adjectives "smouldering" or "brooding." Like they are so concerned with their brand of bankable cool, they become incapable of vulnerability or experimental or — more importantly — human approaches to their performance. In other words, the anti-Robert Pattinson.

It's a hesitancy and complacency that constantly leaves this Hig humbly, cutely smile-shrugging off yet another child calling him her hero. Or impassively racking another round in another dogfight — against an enemy just mean, dirty and unattractive enough to allow the audience to keep affording Hig their sympathies as the unequivocal good guy in all this moral muck.

It's also a framing that allows for a smooth and easy depiction of good and bad, that doesn't challenge its audience to identify with anyone who has realistic, unmarketable depth. It's an overall inoffensive, and oddly lighthearted remaking of a dystopian drama, that goes so far as to remove any troublesome reference to climate change, which was originally peppered through the novel. Its simplicity extends to the sound effects, calling on foley artists to work overtime to seed endearing and plaintive animal-whines throughout the audio track, just in case you forgot to be sympathetic to the cute dog for 30 seconds.

Of course, the movie's issues can't all be laid at Elordi's feet. That would fall more toward writer Mark L. Smith (The Revenant, Twisters), and how-the-mighty-have-fallen director Scott; the creative team that take the film's cliche, but functional, intro and pivot to something both uneven and uninteresting. A plot that increasingly deviates from the book, though in ways that do nothing to reinterpret or reinforce its theme.

A bifurcated storytelling that splits its time between two characters in order to beef up what is essentially an introspective philosophical rumination with Michael Bay-esque battles. A feat of worldbuilding that starts grounded in reality, only to skip to laughably unserious — and at times vaguely offensive — tribes of survivors riding horseback while screaming. All culminating in an equal-parts absurd and visually ugly finale that cements the fact that Smith and Scott lost the plot about an hour ago.

items: Insidious: Out of the Further swaps sadness for terror. Then forgets to terrorize
The End of Oak Street is a fun — but flat — Spielberg clone

blocks.text: Comparing to the source material, things feel even worse. Despite the fact Heller reportedly cried after his first viewing of the film (granted, largely due to just seeing his first novel making it to the big screen), it's impossible to think how poorly this movie understands what made The Dog Stars great.

Partly it is the form, adapting as it does a novel whose story is as much its writing style as Cormac McCarthy's The Road — a book The Dog Stars is infinitely, and understandably, compared to. The script clumsily transitions a narrative written by, and from the perspective of, a poet in a world he can't remember as home, to one that is more concerned with mixing explosions with a truncated love story.

One that takes lines like, "I was a troll who lived at the base of a tree. Looked at the world through a scratchy scrim of needles and branches. Lived on rain, on bits of song and memory," and crafts a movie with no monologue or attempts at insight into the character. In short, a movie that does not understand or respect the purpose or power of language.

blocks.caption: The Dog Stars is set in a post-apocalyptic world, with Hig and his dog flying in their beat-up Cessna. (Fabio Lovino/20th Century Studios/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: But it is also one that, instead of reimagining its message for a new medium, somehow both oversimplifies and misses it. It's a surface-level reading and retelling that had Scott interpret the story as being about self-sufficiency, instead of the opposite.

It's an adaptation that took the story of a man altogether defined by his self-doubt and self-hatred and replaced it with a competency porn flick about a man who just happens to be really good at everything. One that cast straight-talking leading man Elordi as the ostensibly neurotic, fraying lead. All while borrowing the one obvious element of the novel — a general pondering slowness — and assuming that is what gave it a sensation of solemn weight.
The poor direction is not, alone, enough to sink it. But enough to make The Dog Stars one of the most poorly made post-apocalyptic adaptations since World War Z. And that's saying something.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Jackson Weaver is a reporter and film critic for CBC's entertainment news team in Toronto. You can reach him at jackson.weaver@cbc.ca.

articles.title: How teen accounts on Instagram and Facebook are changing after Meta's $18B US settlement
articles.summary: Changes are coming for teen Instagram and Facebook users after parent company Meta agreed to platform changes in a landmark U.S. settlement to resolve claims of online harms to youth. Experts tell…

blocks.text: World

Changes are coming for teen Instagram and Facebook users after parent company Meta agreed to platform changes in a landmark U.S. settlement to resolve claims of online harms to youth. Experts tell CBC News what's changing, how widely and what impact this might have going forward.
'Writing is on the wall for the social media industry,' says analyst
Listen to this article
